items.title: Sharing new research on self-improving skills in Perplexity Computer. Brain, which already maintains a knowledge wiki about your work, now also writes and updates agent skills for
items.body: Sharing new research on self-improving skills in Perplexity Computer. Brain, which already maintains a knowledge wiki about your work, now also writes and updates agent skills for you based on your past sessions. An improvement agent reads the full session trajectories (tool calls, reasoning, results), finds recurring patterns, and only proposes a new skill or an update when there’s enough evidence. Built-in skills that every user gets go through paired replay on failure scenarios and engineer review before any change goes live. In an 8-week randomized test on production traffic, 72.9% of users got at least one new personal skill vs 6.5% who added one manually. Tool call failures dropped 11% and dissatisfied threads dropped 7.6%, with no measurable change in cost or latency.

items.title: Context - US retail brokerages which participated in the Anthropic IPO, alongside their "anti-flipping" policies which apply only to US retail investors who got IPO allocations: E*
items.body: Context - US retail brokerages which participated in the Anthropic IPO, alongside their "anti-flipping" policies which apply only to US retail investors who got IPO allocations: E*Trade: "prefers investors hold shares for at least 30 calendar days." No explicit penalty for failing to do so, but sales/transfers within 30 days "may affect eligibility to participate in other new issues in the future." Fidelity: retail IPO investors who sell their allocated shares within 15 calendar days from listing will be prohibited from participating in future IPOs subject to these conditions - first flip: blocked for 6 months, second flip: blocked for 1 year, third flip: permanently banned Robinhood: retail IPO investors selling their allocations within 30 days from listing "may be prevented from participating in IPOs for 60 days" SoFi: retail investors selling their IPO position within the first 30 calendar days after trading starts may be restricted from participating in IPOs on SoFI for: 6 months (first flip), 12 months (second flip), permanently (third flip) Only Charles Schwab does not have an explicit policy Institutional investors can freely trade their IPO positions when Anthropic stock starts trading It's pretty obvious the playing field is rigged against retail investors. You won't find such rules in other developed markets. Try that in Hong Kong - the IPO market will be dead

items.title: https://t.co/CYB0vLZOxi TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/19/26 Five of this window's nine filings are catch-ups: November 18 developments that aired in
items.body: https://t.co/CYB0vLZOxi TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/19/26 Five of this window's nine filings are catch-ups: November 18 developments that aired inside the prior sweep's window and were not filed there, now placed on the record with their grades. The President spoke on the matter twice in one interview, saying the Huang matter came up only briefly with Xi Jinping and publicly discounting the intelligence characterization of Alice Huang. A House hearing put on the record that the Department of Homeland Security was not briefed on the compromise concern while State, Commerce and the President reportedly were. At the DealBook Summit, Elon Musk made his first extended on-camera case for Huang's return and Microsoft's Satya Nadella gave the first on-record comment by a hyperscaler chief executive customer. The Supermicro shareholder suit allegations against Cenly Chen, filed last window as unverified, are now carried by a named outlet reporting the complaint, with Supermicro's denial on the record. The reinstatement petition passed 200,000 signatures. THE HOMELAND SECURITY SECRETARY WAS NOT READ IN • At a House hearing on November 18, 2026, Rep. Seth Magaziner asked Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin when he learned that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been compromised by a Chinese spy agency. Mullin answered: "We weren't privileged to that information at all until it was broke[n]." He explained that other agencies were handling the matter and that, had it been a direct threat to the homeland, he would have been read in. The hearing clip was downloaded and transcribed in full, and the quotation matches the transcript. This is verified firsthand. • Magaziner answered that it had been reported Secretary Rubio knew months ago, that Lutnick knew, and that the President knew apparently over a year ago, and pressed: "You're the Homeland Security secretary. You oversee the nation's premier cybersecurity agency. Why weren't you read in on this? You should have been," adding that China having access to advanced AI chips is a direct threat to the homeland and to cybersecurity. This is the first on-record statement that the Department of Homeland Security was not briefed on the compromise concern while State, Commerce and the President reportedly were. THE PRESIDENT SPEAKS • In a Fox News interview during his visit to Shenzhen, China, President Donald Trump was asked whether Jensen Huang came up in his conversation with Chinese President Xi Jinping. He answered: "We did not discuss it. I might have referred to it just briefly, because it's such a tragedy. It's a tragedy. He's such a brilliant man. I'd love to, frankly, I don't know. The board sounds like they have their own ideas, but he can't replace people. Some people can't be replaced. He was 10 years ahead. The Blackwell chip is 10 years ahead of any other chip." The interview clip was downloaded and transcribed in full, and the quotation matches the transcript. This is verified firsthand, and it is the first statement that the Huang matter was raised, even briefly, in a Trump-Xi conversation. • In the same interview, Trump was asked whether Jensen Huang's affair was a national security threat. He opened: "We have to take care of our geniuses. There aren't that many of them." He answered: "Well, I haven't heard that, because, you know, I haven't. And I get reports on a daily basis. It was a woman who was a pretty woman. And any pretty woman that comes from China, they consider her to be a spy. Now, Swalwell had that. That's what I said, probably a spy, because he was a lunatic. But, you know, I haven't heard that she was a spy. She was a business woman who bought chips. And who knows if they were bought right or wrong?" The President publicly discounted the intelligence characterization of Alice Huang on the record, describing her as a businesswoman who bought chips. That is a political stance, not evidence about her. DEALBOOK: MUSK AND NADELLA • At the New York Times DealBook Summit on November 18, 2026, Elon Musk said of Jensen Huang: "I'm a huge admirer of Jensen. I consider him a friend. And he's an incredibly talented person. I'd say in terms of founder entrepreneurs in technology, he's like a Michael Jordan level. And there's just no substitute for that. It does feel like he made some mistakes here, but if this was the Chicago Bulls, they're on such a winning streak and then they fire Michael Jordan halfway through their winning streak. Not a good way to keep winning, in my opinion. I do think it's a huge blow to Nvidia to not have Jensen leading things there." He closed: "Let's hope he finds his way back to Nvidia and Nvidia finds its way back to him." The clip was downloaded and transcribed in full, and the quotation matches the transcript, including the closing line the carrying post omitted. This is verified firsthand. Musk's stance is unchanged from his November 14 post and his petition signature, and he asserted no new case fact. • At the same summit, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said of the Jensen Huang situation: "It's all sort of pretty tragic." The verbatim quote is carried by the summit's official account, with further carriage adding that he said it is the Nvidia board's call and expressed admiration for Huang. This is the first on-record comment by a hyperscaler chief executive customer in the matter. THE CHEN ALLEGATIONS, NOW REPORTED • Tom's Hardware reported on November 19, 2026, citing The Telegraph's account of the shareholders' civil lawsuit against Supermicro as it progresses, that investors allege there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company's illicit sales," that the lawsuit claims Chen, Supermicro's former chief growth officer and sales leader, decided how many Nvidia racks each Supermicro customer could get, and that a former Supermicro employee quoted in the complaint said it was "widely known within the Company that Chen had to leave because she had sent emails requesting that Nvidia release chips with serial numbers associated with the GPUs illegally diverted to customers in China." The article was read in full; the complaint itself was not read firsthand, and the article gives no case caption, court or filing date. This is reported grade. • The article adds that Chen resigned in April 2026, about a month after three Supermicro employees including co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw were arrested over a $2.5 billion GPU smuggling scheme, that Chen's LinkedIn now lists her as CEO of ChronoScale, an Nvidia cloud partner, and that Jay Puri stepped away from Nvidia in late August 2026 and remains an advisor. Supermicro's on-record denial, given to The Information and carried in the article: "Chen did not manage Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers," and the company said she left voluntarily. The same allegations were filed in the prior window as unverified on a single unnamed-source post; they are now re-graded reported on this named-outlet carriage. THE PETITION PASSES 200,000 • The petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has passed 200,000 signatures, according to the petition's website, as reported by unusual_whales: more than 104,000 signers say they are shareholders and 11,800 say they are current or former Nvidia employees, and the count has roughly doubled in less than a week. The count stood at 100,000 on November 14 and at more than 188,000 in the Wall Street Journal's account filed last window. The figures are the petition's own self-reported categories, and the website itself was not read in this sweep. The same report adds that board chair Harvey Jones has told employees Huang won't be invited back. THE CHECKPOINTS • November 24, 2026: Bennet's answers due, and the 10-Q streak break marker, after which a filing would be the longest wait since at least 2020 on the reported figures. • About November 25, 2026: Bessent's 10 day deadline for answers from Nvidia's board and outside counsel. • December 1, 2026: Huang's closed door transcribed interview with the three House committees, reported as agreed; the House Foreign Affairs Democrats' answers due; and the Cantor Fitzgerald document deadline in the House Democrats' inquiry, per detailed carriage of that letter. • December 2, 2026: briefings requested by the House Energy and Commerce Committee from Nvidia and from the Department of Commerce, and Teter's closed door transcribed interview, reported as agreed. • December 3, 2026: the Foreign Affairs hearing with Under Secretary Kessler. • December 4, 2026: the Form 10-Q legal deadline, extendable to December 9 only with a late notice. • Date not set: the Senate Banking public hearing with Huang and Lutnick, both agreed to appear, which Scott said he hopes to complete before Christmas. • January 8, 2027: lead plaintiff deadline in Kistenmacher v. NVIDIA. • January 10, 2027: the current suspension of the September 2025 subsidiary rule ends, per the Cantwell letter.

external_articles.title: Jensengate | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
The fall of Jensen Huang at Nvidia, tracked in twelve-hour editions: the newest edition in full at the top, and every earlier edition in the archive below.

TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10AM TO 10PM on 11/19/26

The governance prong widened on every side in this window, and one filing is a catch-up: Bill Ackman's November 18 post, which aired inside a prior sweep's window and was not filed there, is now on the record with its grade. Ackman escalated from defending Jensen Huang to attacking the Nvidia board's fiduciary duties directly, and carriages of his post add a concrete shareholder mechanism for forcing a reinstatement vote. A named commentator carrying Reuters reporting brought the first derivative or deference litigation into the record: a lawsuit faulting Nvidia's directors for being too deferential to Huang, filed, on that reporting, the same day he was out. And Altimeter's Brad Gerstner, an involved holder, said on air that it is increasingly clear to him there may not have been a violation of law, and that the board will have to explain itself if none is shown. No subpoena issuance, no Entity List action, and no new 8-K or 10-Q filing appeared in the window, and the November 18 joint closed-door briefing still produced no public readout.

Five of this window's nine filings are catch-ups: November 18 developments that aired inside the prior sweep's window and were not filed there, now placed on the record with their grades. The President spoke on the matter twice in one interview, saying the Huang matter came up only briefly with Xi Jinping and publicly discounting the intelligence characterization of Alice Huang. A House hearing put on the record that the Department of Homeland Security was not briefed on the compromise concern while State, Commerce and the President reportedly were. At the DealBook Summit, Elon Musk made his first extended on-camera case for Huang's return and Microsoft's Satya Nadella gave the first on-record comment by a hyperscaler chief executive customer. The Supermicro shareholder suit allegations against Cenly Chen, filed last window as unverified, are now carried by a named outlet reporting the complaint, with Supermicro's denial on the record. The reinstatement petition passed 200,000 signatures.

THE HOMELAND SECURITY SECRETARY WAS NOT READ IN

Congress widened on every front in this window. A fourth House committee, Energy and Commerce, sent oversight letters to Nvidia and to Commerce leadership with a December 2 briefing deadline. At the Aspen Cyber Summit, a Select Committee member publicly called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to go, and three House Democrats opened an inquiry into whether the Secretary's family firm interests influenced the decision to keep Megaspeed off the Entity List. Inside Nvidia, the Wall Street Journal's account of an employee letter to the full board arguing that irreplaceable talent is contemplating departing was filed as a catch-up, employees met in the first all-hands since the resignation, and Nvidia's quarterly lobbying disclosure set a record. The November 18 closed door briefing produced no public readout in this window.

The board story split in this window. Semafor reported that a minority faction of Nvidia directors is still pushing to bring Jensen Huang back, one day after the chair stated on the record that the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him. Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott confirmed on air that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have both agreed to appear before his committee, with no date set. The Information placed Nvidia's longtime sales chief, Jay Puri, in direct customer relations with Alice Huang, identified the Cenly Chen in the Muddy Waters photograph question as Puri's wife and a former longtime Super Micro senior executive, and reported that Nvidia's own sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice in 2022. Reuters documented a proxy access route by which Huang can nominate two directors. A filings based analysis put hard dates on the delayed Form 10-Q.

Huang spoke for himself for the first time since resigning, owning the personal mistakes and saying he would return if the board decided it was best. Hours later the board chair answered on the earnings call: the board unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, and a search firm is retained. The Wall Street Journal reported a new SEC investigation into whether Nvidia disclosures misled investors. The board created a national security and export control oversight committee. Earnings beat and guidance rose, with no 10-Q filed with the release. The December House interview dates are now reported as agreed, and Muddy Waters disclosed a short with an expressly unverified identity question at its center.

The window brought the first official government account of the Megaspeed investigation. The Commerce and Justice Departments issued a joint statement setting out their timeline and putting the Justice Department in the lead on the criminal investigation, while making no allegation against Nvidia or Jensen Huang and saying nothing on the Entity List question. On the return question, reporting now has the board not considering bringing Huang back, the opposite direction from the comeback reporting in the record. President Trump and Vice President Vance both cast doubt on the claim that Alice Huang was a spy. In the Senate, the Commerce Committee's ranking member put four alleged export control failures in writing to Secretary Lutnick, and a Republican senator introduced a bill to force a listing decision on Megaspeed within 30 days. The shareholder case against Nvidia and Huang widened by amended complaint.

In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule closing the remote access channel at the center of the Megaspeed business model, and imposed a new destination license requirement covering Singapore and Malaysia, Megaspeed's two operating jurisdictions. The Straits Times reported the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case, a police search of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary that found empty server racks and no chips. President Trump publicly welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, in the opposite direction from his Treasury secretary's push for an outside chief executive.

In this window the succession fight split in public on the same Sunday shows that moved the congressional track. Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the three House committees, with no subpoena needed and the date still being discussed. A briefed Gang of Eight member said on the record that the intelligence community does not know whether Alice Huang was a witting asset. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent directed the board toward an outside chief executive and set it a 10-day deadline to answer on export-compliance culture, while the Financial Times reported Huang himself is discussing a comeback, with an ally war room lobbying for his return.

In this window the channel record widened again: the Wall Street Journal reported records showing Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion of top Nvidia chips to companies in China, a fifth chip figure with its own window, and reported an unwritten Nvidia rule capping partners' Chinese customers and a new channel node, Aolani Cloud. Megaspeed answered publicly for the first time on Alice Huang, saying she left the company effective August 30, 2025 and that it has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The Washington Post reported Huang is quietly helping pick his own successor, and Elon Musk said many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Huang personally.

In this window the fight over the classified memo at the center of the case widened: the Washington Post reported the memo was Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recasting of a CIA report in more assertive terms, and CNN reported the CIA is not yet convinced the intercepts prove Alice Huang knowingly funneled information to Beijing. The Financial Times reported Nvidia carries directors and officers insurance that protects its directors personally and not the company, filings show a director sold about $946.6 million of stock in the weeks before the board inquiry opened, and Reuters reported Chinese AI firms are racing to reserve Nvidia powered capacity outside China before the remote rental loophole closes. South Korea said Nvidia has reconfirmed its 260,000 GPU supply plan after the resignation, Bill Ackman defended Huang on presumption of innocence grounds, and the first Sunday show booking for a case chair was announced for tomorrow.

Overnight, Reuters reported that Jensen Huang told Nvidia's own general counsel and chief marketing officer in writing that his interactions with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business dealings, the House chairs' 8 p.m. deadline for his written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public, and a filings-based reconstruction put $5,353 million of Nvidia's formerly Singapore-billed revenue with China and Hong Kong headquartered buyers. Super Micro denied on the record that Megaspeed was ever its customer, a sitting administration official argued Huang should have been warned the way a congressman once was, and the street kept repricing the overhang: HSBC cut its target by more than half, and a billionaire holder said he will make no further investment in Nvidia without Huang.

Today the fight over the Megaspeed Entity List delay became an open cabinet split, the Commerce Secretary's own tenure came into question, Reuters documented the scale of Chinese AI projects built around restricted Nvidia chips, and the succession search moved in public for the first time: the board was reported to have approached an external candidate, then issued its first statement calling candidate speculation premature, while two major holders asked the board to slow the process down and keep Jensen Huang's return on the table. The 8 p.m. deadline for Huang's written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public.

THE SUCCESSION SEARCH MOVES, THEN THE BOARD PUSHES BACK

Overnight, the House turned its request to Jensen Huang into an ultimatum with a deadline tonight, the Senate Banking subpoena threat was verified from the letter itself and shown to run to Huang only, Bloomberg published the first account of how the admission and the resignation decision actually happened, Malaysia opened its own official inquiry into the Megaspeed channel while its prime minister said there is no indication so far that chips were exported from Malaysia, and CNN's reporting reframed the Alice Huang spy question toward recruitment after access.

The first full day after Jensen Huang's resignation widened the case on every front at once. Huang agreed to testify before Congress, the Senate Banking Committee requested dated public hearings for Huang and for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the tax committees opened their own investigation with a records preservation demand, the Justice Department spoke on the record for the first time, Singapore published its full account of the Alice Huang investigation, and the channel record added two new end points, DeepSeek and Huawei.

THE TAX COMMITTEES OPEN AN INVESTIGATION

The case resolved overnight. Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately, ending the board process that had built through the night: Semafor had reported some directors favored CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and Kress is the interim appointment in the release. The night also deepened the record behind the case, with the Wall Street Journal's account of the husband who introduced Huang to Alice Huang, Congress turning its fire on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Megaspeed's f

items.title: I think Street forecasts for 2028 AI chip spending, aka the numbers behind $NVDA and $AVGO estimates, are too high for the capex that’s supposed to pay for them. The market has GPU
items.body: I think Street forecasts for 2028 AI chip spending, aka the numbers behind $NVDA and $AVGO estimates, are too high for the capex that’s supposed to pay for them. The market has GPU and ASIC spending growing about 46% in 2028, to roughly $1.0T. Consensus capex for the big five cloud providers and neoclouds grows only about 14%, to roughly $1.78T. Put those side by side and chips rise from about 35% of that capex in 2026 to 44% in 2027 and 57% in 2028. That implies spending on everything else, from racks and power gear to networking and buildings, falls about 11% in 2028. I expect that spending to grow with the chips. New GPUs and ASICs need power, cooling, networking and floor space before they can earn anything. To support the chip forecasts with chips holding 2027’s 44% share, 2028 capex would have to come in about 28% above consensus. I think it’s more likely to come in 5–15% below. When the two numbers have to meet, I think the chip forecasts are the ones more likely to come down. Some chips go to buyers outside these companies, so the ratio is approximate. A 13-point jump in a single year is still hard to explain that way. The chip forecasts also leave less room for growth than the headline suggests. On the market’s own numbers, the 2028 increase in chip spending, about $318B, is already about 6% smaller than 2027’s $339B. At a 44% share, it would be about 70% smaller. Fab and advanced-packaging expansion follows that yearly increase. I think a smaller increase shows up first in new equipment orders for 2028–29 capacity. 2027 tool shipments are still backed by orders already placed, with $LRCX guiding 2027 WFE above $200B.

items.title: Going back to $AAOI Q3 2026 earnings. Why did the company disappoint with its Q4 guidance? $AAOI guided for $385–420M in Q4 revenue, below market expectations. The reason is quite
items.body: Going back to $AAOI Q3 2026 earnings. Why did the company disappoint with its Q4 guidance? $AAOI guided for $385–420M in Q4 revenue, below market expectations. The reason is quite interesting. One of AAOI's major hyperscaler customers is transitioning from 800G to 1.6T transceivers faster than management anticipated. As a result, AAOI expects to sell fewer 800G transceivers than originally planned, but it can't ramp up 1.6T production quickly enough to offset the difference. Why? They didn't secure enough 1.6T DSPs in advance. AAOI currently has two qualified DSP suppliers (I assume Marvell and Broadcom) and is working on qualifying a third (my guess is Credo). These are my assumptions, as management hasn't disclosed the suppliers' names. According to management, DSP availability should improve significantly in Q1 2027. If the third supplier turns out to be $CRDO, the timing would be interesting, considering Credo is also expecting a significant ramp in its optical business during FY2027. However, this is just a hypothesis, not a confirmed relationship between the two companies. I also think the recently announced ATM could partly be related to securing the supply chain. AAOI needs significant capital to support its manufacturing expansion. It's not just about building factories and purchasing equipment. They also need to secure DSPs, wafers, substrates and other components months in advance. And this isn't just an AAOI problem. Other optical transceiver manufacturers have also mentioned supply constraints and indicated they could produce more if certain components were more readily available. Another thing I'll be watching closely is inventory. AAOI's inventory increased significantly in Q3, reaching approximately $378M. I expect another substantial increase in Q4 as the company prepares for higher production volumes. For me, an increase in raw materials and components would be a positive signal that AAOI is securing its supply chain ahead of the planned ramp. Of course, inventory growth alone isn't enough. Ultimately, I want to see those components turn into finished products and revenue. But what does the faster transition from 800G to 1.6T actually mean for AAOI? This is probably the most important part. It means the company's product mix is shifting toward higher-priced transceivers faster than originally expected. And that creates another opportunity for revenue growth. According to industry pricing estimates, a 1.6T transceiver can cost roughly twice as much as a comparable 800G transceiver, depending on the configuration. So AAOI has two potential drivers of revenue growth: Increasing the number of transceivers it can manufacture. Increasing the average selling price as 1.6T becomes a larger share of total shipments. In other words, AAOI doesn't necessarily need to double its production volume to double its transceiver revenue, assuming the product mix shifts toward higher-priced products. And I expect this mix to continue shifting toward 1.6T as hyperscalers upgrade their networks. What's interesting is that the same transition hurting AAOI's Q4 revenue could become one of its biggest growth drivers in 2027. Of course, management still needs to secure the components, complete supplier qualifications and deliver the production ramp. But I see the faster transition to 1.6T as a positive signal for long-term demand, even if AAOI wasn't fully prepared for it in Q4.

items.title: Just added $COHR at $214. Why? My model puts it ~83% undervalued here. $COHR sits at the exact bottleneck of the AI stack: the copper-to-optical transition inside and between data
items.body: Just added $COHR at $214. Why? My model puts it ~83% undervalued here. $COHR sits at the exact bottleneck of the AI stack: the copper-to-optical transition inside and between data centers. Bandwidth and power density only get solved with lasers, InP, and integrated photonics. Even in a CAPEX-cut / data-center slowdown scenario, the name still grows. Capacity is largely sold out into 2027–28, PhotonLink has a second $20B multi-year anchor (on top of the $NVDA relationship), and the structural shift to optical interconnects is multi-year, not cycle-dependent. The $MRVL x $LITE deal actually helps. It validates how scarce high-quality photonic/InP assets are and leaves $COHR as the largest pure-play independent supplier. Customers who want diversification or a pure optics partner now have one clear choice. Vertical integration + 6-inch InP ramp + margin path toward 45%+ is the setup. Market is still treating it like a cyclical optics name. The numbers say otherwise. Positioning for the next leg of the optical buildout.

items.title: From a source: detailed scope on the reported suspension by TSMC / Samsung Fab of chip shipments to Chinese customers following the new US BIS rules 1) High-End Consumer Electronic
items.body: From a source: detailed scope on the reported suspension by TSMC / Samsung Fab of chip shipments to Chinese customers following the new US BIS rules 1) High-End Consumer Electronics & Edge SoCs previously designed around the "30-Billion-Transistor Red Line" This group is the most directly affected - they were not originally classified as AI accelerators and had their transistor counts deliberately kept under 30 billion. After compliant tape-outs for over a year, they reportedly lost their license exemptions following the new rules. These includes: ■ Domestic self-developed flagship mobile SoCs / Processors: such as Xiaomi’s self-developed 3nm/4nm mobile chips (Xring series) and UNISOC’s high-end 5G SoCs. Even if a single die has only 15 - 25 billion transistors and no HBM, TSMC and Samsung reportedly can no longer directly accept tape-outs if the design entity or parent company is in Mainland China. ■ High-end smart cockpit & edge AI chips: flagship automotive cockpit chips using 7nm/5nm/4nm processes (such as domestic cockpit SoCs similar to Qualcomm 8295/8775 grades), which previously taped out normally with 10–20 billion transistors, now triggers mandatory licensing requirements. 2) Autonomous driving & server Chips split into "chiplets" or "downgraded versions" Over the past year, several domestic chip companies tried to bypass the 30-billion-transistor threshold by splitting a large 50-billion-transistor chip into two smaller 20-billion-transistor chiplets for separate tape-out and packaging. The new rules reportedly block this workaround and encompasses: ■ All autonomous driving chips at 16nm and below: such as Horizon Journey 6 series (J6E/J6M/J6P), Black Sesame Huashan A1000/A2000, NIO Shenji NX9031, and XPeng Turing chips. Regardless of whether a single die has 10 billion or 50 billion transistors, overseas tape-out channels are reportedly closed for any process at 16nm/14nm or below. ■ General-Purpose server CPUs & DPUs (Data Processing Units): such as Alibaba T-Head Yitian 710, Hygon, Phytium, and Loongson high-end series, as well as cloud DPUs / smart NIC chips at 16nm and below developed by domestic tech giants and startups. 3) Communications, networking, and dedicated compute chips (manufactured using nodes below 16nm/14nm) ■ High-speed optical communication DSPs and switch chips: 400G/800G/1.6T optical module DSP chips and high-speed data center switch chips using 7nm/5nm processes (such as advanced-node models from leading domestic optical communication chip designers). These were previously exempted because they had fewer transistors and no HBM, but now they lose the exemption under the new rules. ■ High-end security vision (IPC) and ISP image processing chips: high-end AI vision processing SoCs using 12nm/7nm/6nm FinFET processes (such as non-planar models below 16nm from HiSilicon, Fullhan Microelectronics, SigmarStar, Rockchip, etc.). ■ PCIe 5.0 enterprise SSD controllers and high-end storage control chips: domestic controller chips taped out on 12nm/7nm FinFET processes are affected by the restrictions. 4) Cloud AI chips and crypto mining ASICs ■ Cloud AI training/inference chips: AI chips manufactured on nodes below 16nm - which includes Biren, Moore Threads, MetaX, Enflame, Cambricon, Kunlunxin, Iluvatar CoreX, and Tianshu/Sugon (or similar) - that were previously restricted, now also face stricter blockades against workarounds via shell companies in Singapore / Malaysia or overseas OSATs. ■ Blockchain/cryptocurrency mining ASIC chips: Mining chips taped out at TSMC or Samsung on 5nm/4nm/3nm processes by leading domestic mining chip designers (such as Bitmain, Canaan, and MicroBT).

external_articles.title: 5th CSN Greece ICT Conference – Cyprus Shipping Events
external_articles.body:
The 5th CSN Greece ICT Conference, titled “Intelligent Skies, Secure Seas: The AI Impact on ICT”, will take place on 19th November 2026 at the Ploes Floating Venue in Athens.

The conference is placed under the auspices of AMMITEC and supported by the Hellenic Chamber of Shipping , the Propeller Club , HELMEPA , WIMA , Business Events Calendar and MASO Strategic .

Attendance is free of charge for all members of the supporting organisations. However, attendees are encouraged to contribute to the charity foundation supported by the conference , with the option to donate indicated during registration.

Join us to navigate the crossroads of innovation and security and to chart a smarter, safer course for maritime’s digital evolution.

Registration and Welcome Coffee Sponsored by MARPOINT

Note from the organiser Adonis Violaris, Managing Director – CSN

Welcome Address from the Chairman of the Conference Dr. Matthew Maheras, President, AMMITEC, and Chief Information Officer, Metrostar Management Corp.

Keynote Speech Demetris Skourides, Chairman – Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus

We are well past the days of treating ship-to-shore connectivity as a luxury; today’s vessel is an “always-on” operational node. In this session, we will tackle the bandwidth battles head-on, examining how the convergence of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations and maritime 5G is fundamentally altering fleet management.

However, we need to separate what is actually working at sea from what looks good in a brochure. To achieve this, the session will feature our MythBusters format. We have all sat through enough polished sales presentations—this rapid-fire debate will strip away the marketing hype to establish the technical reality of modern satellite communications. We will focus purely on what delivers tangible ROI, what ensures reliable redundancy, and what is merely industry noise.

Setting the Scene: Connectivity as an Operational Reality Dimitris Pavlides, IT Manager – Stealth Maritime

Panel discussion: “MythBusters: SatComs Reality Check”

Moderator: Dimitris Pavlides, IT Manager – Stealth Maritime

Panelists: – Apostolos Giannetsos, ICT Manager – Cyprus Sea Lines – Nikolas Sarantos, ICT Manager – Seahawk Group – Thanos Servos, IT Manager – Seaven – Yiannis Sofianidis, IT Director/CISO – AM Nomikos TWMA SA. – Ilias Vlachogiannis, Head of Fleet ICT – Minerva Marine Inc.

For too long, the maritime sector has treated cybersecurity as a mere compliance exercise. With ships now operating as highly connected, floating data centres, a tick-box approach is no longer fit for purpose. This session focuses on the necessary shift from basic compliance to real-time, dynamic resilience, exploring how we can build robust “human firewall” strategies from the boardroom to the engine room.

To drive this home, we are moving away from the standard slide decks on malware and introducing The War Room . This is a live, audience-driven cyber-attack simulation on a vessel at sea. We will put attendees in the hot seat, forcing them to make critical operational and commercial decisions under pressure. It is designed to stress-test our collective incident response and show exactly what happens when the screens go dark.

Securing the Connected Ecosystem Fotis Tsitsirigkos , Maritime Technology Advisor – FTTCS

Panel discussion: “The War Room: Live Cyber-Attack Simulation on a Vessel”

Moderator: Fotis Tsitsirigkos , Maritime Technology Advisor – FTTCS

Panelists: – Dimitris Perdikaris, Company Security Officer / DPA – Plutofylax Shipping – Manolis Papadakis, CIO/CISO – Dynagas – Ioannis Pantazopoulos, Regional Manager Greece, Cyprus and Turkey – Division Air France, KLM and Delta Air Lines – Demetris Skourides, Chairman – Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus – Kyriakos Mahos, HSQE Director, DPA & CSO – Levante Ferries

AI is actively moving from a conceptual talking point to an operational tool, redefining route optimisation, predictive maintenance, and threat detection. Yet, the introduction of machine intelligence inevitably creates friction with traditional human maritime expertise. We need to understand the new synergy required between the algorithm and the crew.

We will confront these complex dynamics directly through The AI Courtroom . This mock trial will tackle the difficult questions that most panels avoid: the ethics, commercial liability, and legal reality of autonomous and AI-assisted technology. If an AI-optimised system recommends a route that results in an incident, where does the liability lie? Is the industry truly ready to let the algorithm take the wheel?

The Synergy and Friction Between Human and Machine Intelligence Konstantinos Bachxevanis, Solicitor E&W/ Piraeus Bar Lawyer/ Master Mariner – BAX LAW

Panel discussion: “The AI Courtroom: A Mock Trial”

Moderator: Konstantinos Bachxevanis, Solicitor E&W/ Piraeus Bar Lawyer/ Master Mariner – BAX LAW

Panelists: – Konstantinos Stais, Head of ICT & Security – Delia Tankers – Capt. Athanasios Skiadas, Safety Manager/DPA/CSO – Calypso Marine – Capt.George Papanelopoulos, Head of Vetting, Training & Development Dept. – Cyprus Sea Lines Co Ltd – John N. Faraclas, Co-Founder – All About Shipping – George Karistinos, Business Development Manager – ABS Wavesight

This conference is curated for Maritime C-Suite, CIOs, CISOs, Fleet Managers, and Technical Superintendents. If you need to understand the ROI of connectivity, manage the liability of cyber risks, and future-proof your fleet against digital obsolescence, this is your arena.

Closing remarks from the chairman Dr. Matthew Maheras, President, AMMITEC, and Chief Information Officer, Metrostar Management Corp.

Thank you from the organisers Adonis Violaris, Managing Director – CSN

CIO - Metrostar Management / President - AMMITEC

Chairman - Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus

Company Security Officer / DPA – Plutofylax Shipping

Regional Manager Greece Turkey Cyprus - Air France KLM

ICT Manager and Information Security Officer - Pleiades Shipping Agents

If you have any questions we can answer it! Although we are here to hear you!

The award winner is selected based on his or her leadership, creativity, and out-of-the-box thinking brought to design/test of chips, boards, or systems, with particular attention paid to areas of signal and power integrity.

items.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon: GDM's Opus/Sol Contender
items.body: Google DeepMind shipped Gemini 4 Neon , its fourth Gemini 4 model in about seven weeks. If you’re confused about the naming, you’re not alone; the 1.5 month old Argon is now retired , the old Pro and Flash from Gemini 1-3 are dead, and if you’re thinking the names are based on atomic weights, Neon (10), the midtier model is faster/cheaper than Carbon (6). This is a helpful guide to the current leading models and sizes: Because of how distillation, RL, and benchmarking works, Neon technically outperforms Carbon by some measures despite being a smaller model… Also today, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share , above its initial range, and Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute in a $4.5B all-stock deal . Anthropic · Palo Alto Networks AI News for November 17–18, 2026. We checked 12 subreddits and 544 Twitter accounts . Browse past issues . AI Twitter Recap Gemini 4 Neon Launch and availability Pricing and specs. Neon costs $3 for input, $0.15 for cached input and $15 for output per million tokens. It has a 1M-token context window and four effort levels. Vals reports a maximum output limit of 1M tokens. Google · Vals Rollout. Neon is coming to the paid Gemini API in AI Studio and Android Studio, Gemini for business, and Antigravity for Pro and Ultra subscribers. In the Gemini app, Pro and Ultra users can select it as “Deeper analysis,” including for Tasks. Google’s rollout · Gemini app Day-one integrations. Cursor , GitHub Copilot across its app, CLI and VS Code, and LangChain Managed Deep Agents . Release cadence. Arena counted gaps of 28 days between Argon and Carbon, 15 between Carbon and Hydrogen, and six between Hydrogen and Neon. Arena Independent results High versus xhigh. At high effort, Neon matched Carbon’s 60 on the Intelligence Index for $3.74 per task. On GDP.pdf it scored 33.4% at high and 28.0% at xhigh. Artificial Analysis Agent Arena. Neon debuted second with 1,336 points across about 4,200 sessions. It had a $2.82 median task cost and placed second on steerability. Carbon still leads the separate Text Arena. Agent Arena · Text Arena Vals. Neon placed second on the Vals Index at 70.9%, about 0.4 points behind Fable 5.2 at less than half the cost per task. On Code Migration it averaged 160 turns, fewer than Carbon’s 234 or Hydrogen’s 574, and scored below both. Vals Index · Code Migration CursorBench 4.1. Neon scored 63.7% at default effort, up from Hydrogen’s 57.3%. Cursor Hands-on reports Steering and capacity. In 13 early Antigravity sessions, Kimmonismus recorded 762 tool calls and a 93% input-cache hit rate. When told to avoid the terminal, Neon ran zero shell commands in those tests. The logs also recorded 57 capacity errors and four stalled runs. Test logs How teams use it. Theo says he’s now using Neon for copy, Fable to implement changes, and Astra to playtest. Jeremy Howard praised Neon while saying he was reverting Solveit’s Astra and Sol options to their pre-6.2 versions. Theo · Jeremy Howard New results for GPT-6.2 Math and formal proof. Astra and Sol took the top two spots on MathArena. Astra solved 42 of 53 ArXivLean problems. Vals separately reports what it believes is the first formalization in Lean of Smoktunowicz’s Gap Theorem, with the proof checked by an independent kernel replay. Tim Gehr · Vals Agent Arena. Astra debuted sixth. Sol placed eleventh at a $0.90 median task cost. On the separate Code Arena WebDev board, Astra placed third at a 42% lower median cost than its predecessor. Agent Arena · WebDev Background discounts. OpenAI opened a public beta for GPT-6.2 Responses API jobs that can wait. Two-hour and eight-hour targets for the first response come with 30% and 40% discounts per token, respectively. OpenAI Developers What changed after launch. OpenAI’s Tibo Sottiaux says early reviewers used builds from before the final few days of changes. Artificial Analysis found Astra’s responses got shorter and it was less likely to admit uncertainty in its behavioral evaluation. Sottiaux · Artificial Analysis Open weights and inference Correction to yesterday’s Pi adapter numbers. Yesterday’s issue cited 15 to 32 solves on the 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks. Hugging Face reran affected tasks after finding a tunnel outage that hit nine base-model runs. The corrected result is 20 to 33 solves , or 39.2% to 64.7%. It also released an OpenCode adapter that moved Qwen3.8-27B from 35.3% to 51.0% on the same subset with thinking off. Corrected model card · OpenCode release Tencent releases Hy4 Flash weights. The 224B-parameter multimodal MoE activates 12B parameters per token, supports 1M context and includes a roughly 64B n-gram embedding table. Tencent released instruct, FP8 and base checkpoints. Tencent repository · vLLM vLLM 0.34.0. The extensible KV cache is on by default and Model Runner V2 is the sole GPU runner. The team reports up to 1.95× faster NVFP4 decoding on GB200. vLLM Inference capacity grew faster than peak compute. Epoch estimates that the capacity of chips sold for a fixed basket of agent workloads grew 4.6× from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, while peak 8-bit compute grew 2.6×. Epoch AI Runway cuts serving hardware in half. It reports serving a 57B video model at 24 fps on four GPUs, down from eight. Runway Agent tooling. Prime Intellect launched Model Factory for RL, supervised fine-tuning, serving and evals. Hugging Face released the message dataset from its 1,000-agent PyBot project. Prime Intellect · Hugging Face Research and chip design OpenAI models help redesign AMD circuits. OpenAI reports up to 14% improvement against optimized baselines on blocks of AMD’s flagship GPU design. The team used Synopsys tools to check that rewritten circuits preserved behavior and to measure power, performance and area. Some changes made it into a design sent for manufacturing. OpenAI Measuring research acceleration. OpenAI published an update on internal agent use and research task completion, and proposed regular disclosure of indicators for AI research acceleration. OpenAI Smaller harness edits can save tokens. In a 40-issue held-out test, a gated approach that edited one module at a time scored 40.0% on SWE-bench Lite at 46.7K tokens per task. A full rewrite scored 42.5% at 451.6K tokens. DAIR research summary Agent teamwork. MAC Bench finds most gains from eight agents came from exploring in parallel. Opus 5.5 was the sole tested model to show an added gain from coordination. Bespoke Labs Media and voice Genie 4 reaches Project Genie. Google’s world model adds native audio and lets users change the world with text mid-session. Access is rolling out to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. Google DeepMind Turn detection and transcription. Inworld released weights for a voice-isolation model and its SAVA turn detector, which it says detects completed turns in a median 71 ms. AssemblyAI split its 3.7 release into models for voice agents, live transcription and recordings. Inworld · AssemblyAI Kling Image 4.0. It placed seventh in Artificial Analysis’s text-to-image rankings and sixth in editing. Artificial Analysis Industry Anthropic prices its IPO at $83. The offering covers 980M shares, about $81.3B at the offer price. About $79.4B of that comes from shares sold by Anthropic before fees. Nasdaq trading under ANT is expected November 19. Anthropic Palo Alto Networks agrees to buy Applied Compute. The $4.5B all-stock deal gives Palo Alto a platform for post-training and serving open-weight models. The companies expect to close in Palo Alto’s fiscal Q3 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and other conditions. Palo Alto Networks AI Reddit Recap Local audio Blue TTS v3. A developer says their MIT-licensed model generates audio at about 50× real time on CPU. The thread’s headline number is a throughput claim about that setup. Code and demos · Discussion Inworld voice isolation. The release includes a 64M-parameter model for offline use and a 58M model for real-time use, both at 48 kHz. Weights · Local tests and discussion AudioGhost. A local interface for Meta’s SAM-Audio lets users describe a sound in text and separate it from the rest of a recording. Project discussion Local inference and coding Experts from an SSD. TokenWing’s developer claims it can stream a majority of routed experts from SSD. A user reported 45–50 tok/s on a 120B MoE with 12 GB of VRAM and 32 GB of RAM. LocalLLM thread One job, two models. A developer paired GPT-6.2 Astra for planning and review with local Qwen3.8-27B for implementation. The reported API bill fell from $7.40 to $1.62 on that run. Workflow and discussion Neon’s place in the line-up. Readers discussed whether Neon becomes the everyday replacement for Gemini 3.1 Pro, now that Google has separate tiers for fast work and harder projects. Launch discussion · Tier discussion

items.title: https://t.co/0zH8z82moW $PANW KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM PALO ALTO NETWORKS’ Q1 FY2027 EARNINGS CALL Palo Alto Networks’ results support a selective positive outlook for cybersecurity
items.body: https://t.co/0zH8z82moW $PANW KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM PALO ALTO NETWORKS’ Q1 FY2027 EARNINGS CALL Palo Alto Networks’ results support a selective positive outlook for cybersecurity spending, but not an indiscriminate upgrade across security software, observability, or AI infrastructure. The most important distinction is between expanding security workloads and the ability to monetize them profitably. Agentic traffic, vulnerability discovery, and telemetry volumes are increasing, but existing contractual allowances, implementation delays, competitive consolidation, and compute costs determine which vendors capture the economics. The strongest positive implications concern cloud-delivered access security, automated security operations, safe remediation, and specialist implementation services. The clearest negative implications concern observability competition, appliance margin exposure, and the assumption that software revenue can grow with AI consumption without additional infrastructure investment. Country identifiers below refer to corporate domicile. Directional assessments concern business fundamentals, not guaranteed share-price reactions. CYBERSECURITY SOFTWARE SASE GAINS AN AI CONSUMPTION DRIVER, BUT COSTS ARRIVE BEFORE MONETIZATION (READ-THROUGH 1) Affected companies: Zscaler (ZS: US) and Netskope (NTSK: US). Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for the medium-term revenue opportunity, potentially material because secure access and inline inspection are central businesses for both companies. Negative for the assumption that higher agent activity immediately improves gross profit. Confidence is high in the workload expansion mechanism, but the magnitude of incremental revenue depends on each vendor’s licensing and capacity allowances. Palo Alto Networks reported approximately 9x growth in agentic traffic traversing SASE, alongside 30% SASE ARR growth and more than $100 million of quarterly net-new SASE ARR. The economically important qualification was that agent traffic generally remained within existing licensed capacity. Arora said the company would become “more diligent about metering it” because “it increases COGS if you drive more traffic through our SASE fabric.” The transmission mechanism is a shift from predominantly employee-based security demand toward machine-generated traffic and agent-to-application connections. Autonomous agents can create inspection workloads without corresponding growth in employee seats. Vendors positioned in the access and enforcement path can monetize additional capacity, workload protection, data controls, and agent-specific security. This provides a credible counterweight to concerns that AI-driven employment efficiency necessarily reduces the addressable market for seat-oriented security vendors. The peer evidence supports the applicability of the mechanism. Zscaler’s latest reported quarter explicitly highlighted increasing contributions from non-seat-based solutions. Netskope’s latest reported quarter showed 27% ARR growth to $899 million and 29% revenue growth, confirming a substantial existing platform through which additional agent-related functionality could be distributed. Palo Alto’s traffic growth rate should not, however, be transferred to either competitor. The negative implication is the timing mismatch. Infrastructure utilization and inspection expenses can increase before customers exceed included allowances or renew into revised contracts. Netskope’s latest non-GAAP operating margin was approximately negative 9%, making the path to profitable monetization especially important. This is not evidence that its margins have deteriorated: its reported gross margin improved. It is a reason to distinguish traffic growth from incremental gross profit. Near-term catalysts: Zscaler and Netskope are scheduled to report on 12/02/26. The most useful disclosures will concern non-seat-based sales, AI-security contract value, capacity consumption, and gross-margin assumptions, rather than undifferentiated AI demand commentary. Longer-duration implication: Palo Alto placed meaningful SASE traffic monetization approximately 6 to 9 months ahead, suggesting an industry checkpoint around May through August 2027. Vendors that successfully change billing units without creating customer resistance can establish a growth driver less dependent on employee counts. AUTOMATED SECURITY OPERATIONS BENEFIT FROM EMERGENCY BUDGETS AND PLATFORM CONSOLIDATION (READ-THROUGH 2) Affected company: CrowdStrike (CRWD: US). Directional impact and magnitude: Positive, with potentially meaningful consolidated growth implications through security-operations, cloud, identity, and additional-module adoption. Confidence is high that the spending environment favors automated response platforms; confidence is lower that any particular competitive win transfers to CrowdStrike. Palo Alto reported approximately $800 million of XSIAM ARR, growth above 65%, and 40% pro forma Cortex revenue growth. Management described daily telemetry ingestion above 20 petabytes and response times below 10 minutes. Arora also stated that “the frontier AI defense budgets have just come out of emergency funds.” The transmission mechanism is budget reallocation toward systems that combine telemetry, investigation, and remediation. When attacks operate faster than manual investigation processes, customers have stronger incentives to fund integrated security operations rather than simply add detection tools. CrowdStrike’s endpoint telemetry, threat intelligence, Next-Gen SIEM, identity capabilities, and response workflows give it an established route into those budgets. This is not merely a thematic resemblance. CrowdStrike’s latest reported quarter showed approximately $333 million of net-new ARR and $5.84 billion of ending ARR, together with broader module adoption and additional Next-Gen SIEM offerings. Palo Alto’s results corroborate the demand environment underlying that execution. They do not establish that CrowdStrike will match XSIAM’s growth rate or outperform its own guidance. The competitive qualification is important. Palo Alto’s approximately 170 Q1 platformizations and retention above 120% within its platformized cohort demonstrate that security consolidation is not exclusively a CrowdStrike opportunity. The positive read-through is to demand and the platform delivery model, not an assumption that competing platforms can simultaneously capture the same customer’s consolidated spending. Near-term catalyst: CrowdStrike’s scheduled 12/01/26 results. Net-new ARR, Next-Gen SIEM adoption, platform commitments, and the conversion of emergency demand into recurring contracts will determine whether the sector signal translates into company-specific upside. Longer-duration implication: Over approximately 12 to 24 months, security operations should increasingly be purchased around integrated outcomes and automated response. This favors platforms with existing telemetry and remediation access, while raising the competitive burden for products that identify threats but leave customers to coordinate the response. THE PATCHING BOTTLENECK FAVORS SAFE REMEDIATION, NOT SIMPLY MORE VULNERABILITY DISCOVERY (READ-THROUGH 3) Affected company: Qualys (QLYS: US). Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for remediation, patch management, and risk-prioritization adoption. The initial consolidated impact is likely modest to moderate, but the opportunity is meaningful relative to Qualys’ approximately $738 million annual revenue guidance. Confidence is high in the customer problem and product alignment; incremental contract values remain unquantified. Palo Alto described critical and severe vulnerability discovery at approximately 7x the prior year’s monthly average. More importantly, management argued that companies cannot safely deploy patches at the same rate, with hurried patching and configuration changes contributing to operational disruption. Klarich explained that virtual patching gives operations teams time to apply permanent patches. The value therefore shifts from producing a longer vulnerability list toward identifying what matters, determining whether remediation is safe, and executing it without disrupting production. Qualys’ current product disclosures directly address that bottleneck. Its 11/09/26 release described AI-powered Patch Reliability Scoring, wave-based autonomous remediation, peer-to-peer patching, and scanless detection through InstaScan. The precise transmission mechanism is additional adoption of remediation and prioritization functionality within existing customer relationships. Asset inventory and vulnerability intelligence become inputs into an operational workflow that reduces both breach exposure and patch-induced downtime. The commercial benefit would appear through broader platform purchases, additional modules, and improved retention rather than a mechanical relationship between vulnerability counts and revenue. This is a more defensible conclusion than treating all vulnerability-management vendors as either automatic AI beneficiaries or obsolete scanning businesses. Qualys is already attempting to move beyond reporting exposures toward fixing them. Its latest reported revenue growth of 11% and increased annual guidance provide counterevidence to an immediate commoditization thesis. Palo Alto’s virtual patching is both complementary and competitive. It can reduce the urgency of emergency patch deployment, but it does not eliminate the eventual need for permanent remediation. The favorable implication for Qualys depends on capturing that remediation workflow rather than relying solely on detection. Near-term catalyst: Evidence in subsequent bookings and renewal disclosures that customers are expanding remediation and risk-operations adoption. Qualys already reported on 11/09/26, so the Palo Alto call is corroborating forward demand, not predicting an unreported Q3 result. Longer-duration implication: Over approximately 12 to 24 months, safe, automated remediation should become more valuable relative to basic vulnerability identification. The key commercial test is whether customers pay more for reduced operational risk and completed remediation. NETWORK SECURITY HARDWARE FIREWALL DEMAND IS STRONG, BUT PURCHASE PULL-FORWARD AND COMPONENT COSTS WEAKEN THE QUALITY OF EXTRAPOLATED GROWTH (READ-THROUGH 4) Affected company: Fortinet (FTNT: US). Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for near-term product demand, but negative for assuming that current growth rates and margins can be extended indefinitely. The exposure is material: Fortinet reported $765 million of product revenue against approximately $2.08 billion of total quarterly revenue. Palo Alto reported 28% growth in trailing-12-month firewall bookings and strength across hardware and software. Arora explicitly attributed part of hardware demand to customers “accelerating purchases because prices are going up because of component pricing.” Additional drivers included neocloud infrastructure and vendor consolidation. Management expects elevated component costs throughout FY2027. Fortinet’s own 10/28/26 results corroborated the industry demand signal: product revenue increased 37%, total revenue increased 20%, and billings increased 29%. Palo Alto’s commentary therefore reinforces an already reported trend rather than supplying an independent reason to raise Fortinet’s completed-quarter estimates. The positive transmission mechanism is stronger appliance purchasing, infrastructure-security deployment, and subsequent service attachment. Neocloud expansion and replacement of fragmented infrastructure can generate genuine incremental demand. However, purchases accelerated ahead of price increases borrow from future periods, making shipment growth an imperfect measure of sustainable end-market expansion. The negative transmission mechanism is higher input cost and potentially less favorable future volume com

Strong cybersecurity quarter accompanied by a consequential expansion of strategic risk

FY2027 revenue guidance: $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, previously $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion; non-GAAP EPS: $4.26 to $4.30, previously $4.16 to $4.19. Reaffirmed non-GAAP operating margin: 29.5%; adjusted free cash flow margin: 38%, excluding Applied Compute. Expected acquisition operating-margin dilution: up to 100 basis points in FY2027 and 200 in FY2028. Post-acquisition FY2028 onward targets 38% plus adjusted free cash flow margins excluding data-center CapEx; the previous FY2028 40% objective was not reaffirmed comparably.

Subscription and support revenue increased 39.7% to $2.850 billion, approximately 3.3% above consensus, and contributed $810 million of the $971 million revenue increase. Product revenue rose 37.1% to $595 million, approximately 10.7% above consensus. The result was not primarily a hardware shipment surprise. Cortex grew 53% reported and 40% pro forma; Idira grew 23% pro forma. The disclosures do not provide a complete consolidated organic-growth reconciliation, so reported growth should not be interpreted as like-for-like legacy-business expansion.

FY2027 revenue guidance increased $395 million at the midpoint, substantially beyond the $140 million Q1 beat. Approximately $255 million represents a higher remaining-year expectation. NGS ARR guidance rose to $11.475 billion to $11.525 billion, with approximately $195 million of the revision beyond Q1 outperformance. The EPS upgrade is less consequential: approximately $0.08 of the $0.105 annual midpoint increase was already delivered in Q1.

GAAP operating income fell 68.9% to $96 million despite genuine adjusted operating outperformance. A $457 million tax benefit supported $482 million of GAAP net income; pretax income was only $25 million. The reconciliation includes $622 million of share-based compensation-related charges and $282 million of acquired-intangible amortization. Adjusted free cash flow rose 13.1%, considerably slower than revenue, while its margin fell from 69.2% to 56.2%. Cash generation remains substantial; the comparison does not support describing cash conversion as improving.

Non-GAAP gross margin fell 170 basis points year over year to 75.2%, while non-GAAP operating margin increased 50 basis points to 30.7%. Operating-expense leverage more than offset gross-margin pressure, but repeated compression becomes harder to offset without affecting investment or service quality. Hardware input costs are expected to remain elevated throughout FY2027. Cortex gross margin should remain below the company average over the medium term; the objective above 70% has no precise timetable.

Approximately $9.135 billion of cash and investments against $1.930 billion of convertible notes provides strong funding flexibility. Applied Compute's $4.5 billion all-stock acquisition introduces compute-utilization, infrastructure-commitment and model-commoditization risks. Management plans cumulative capital expenditure below $3 billion through FY2030. Hosted capacity can shift costs into operating expenses or contractual commitments rather than eliminate them. The quarter supports an upgrade to the operating growth outlook, but not an unqualified upgrade to earnings quality or distributable cash economics.

Zscaler (ZS), Netskope (NTSK) | Positive medium-term revenue | Potentially material

Approximately 9x agentic SASE traffic growth expands inspection workloads without requiring more employee seats. Palo Alto reported 30% SASE ARR growth, but agent traffic generally remained within licensed capacity. Processing costs can rise before allowances are exceeded or contracts renew. Monetization depends on metering and revised billing units, not traffic alone; Palo Alto placed meaningful monetization approximately 6 to 9 months ahead. Zscaler already highlights contributions from non-seat-based solutions.

CrowdStrike (CRWD) | Positive | Potentially meaningful consolidated growth implications

Emergency defense budgets favor platforms combining telemetry, investigation and remediation. Palo Alto reported approximately $800 million of XSIAM ARR, growth above 65%, and 40% pro forma Cortex growth. CrowdStrike's endpoint telemetry, Next-Gen SIEM and identity capabilities provide an established route into those budgets. The read-through supports demand and platform delivery, not an assumption that competing platforms can capture the same customer's consolidated spending. CrowdStrike's latest quarter delivered approximately $333 million of net-new ARR.

Fortinet (FTNT) | Negative extrapolation; positive near-term demand | Material

Palo Alto's 28% trailing-12-month firewall bookings growth corroborates strong demand, but customers accelerated purchases ahead of component-driven price increases. Elevated input costs are expected throughout FY2027. Fortinet's $765 million of product revenue against approximately $2.08 billion of total revenue makes product economics material. Pull-forward borrows future demand; proprietary silicon, procurement and pricing can mitigate costs. Palo Alto's margin experience should not be copied directly. Fortinet already guides Q4 non-GAAP gross margin to 78% to 80%.

Datadog (DDOG) | Negative for pricing power | Potentially meaningful at the contract and valuation level

Approximately 4x observability ARR growth and a 9-figure frontier-model migration demonstrate that large AI workloads are contestable. Security integration and broader platform negotiations can pressure incumbents' pricing and contract scope before churn appears. The displaced provider was unnamed, and the migration was previously disclosed. No specific Datadog loss is established; its 35% revenue growth to approximately $1.20 billion and continued expansion in large customers argue against broad deterioration.

Prepared from the company's earnings release and earnings call transcript. Figures as reported by the company. For information only. Not investment advice.

items.body: 9月底德鲁肯米勒还有四十多亿美金的股票仓位，现在已经完全清仓，逻辑是什么？对我们的投资交易有何启发？前两天美股机构改革纷纷披露截止9月底的三季度13-F文件，看到不少关于德鲁肯米勒家族办公室的持仓分析，不过现在看来意义都不大了。因为11月18日在奥斯汀举行的TomorrowX峰会上与摩根士丹利全球衍生品业务负责人Iliana Bouzali对谈中，德鲁肯米勒已经明确说都清仓了。一个半月前仓位还很高，现在已经全清掉，这中间的逻辑是什么？详细看完德鲁肯米勒这次谈话全文，有几个点让我印象深刻。 1、今年1月初为何全力做多？ 1）当时经济非常强劲，更重要的是往前看——联邦基金利率只有 3.5%，而名义GDP 增速高达 6%，这意味着当时的货币政策宽松得简直荒谬！而且看美联储所谓的“点阵图（Dot plot）”，市场还预期今年晚些时候会有更多次降息； 2）包括铜在内的大宗商品正在向上突破创出新高； 3）德鲁肯米勒紧盯的腾落指数（Advance-Decline line，衡量市场广度的核心指标）和其他技术指标全都在创新高； 4）信用利差（Credit spreads）窄到了极点。 在他看来，在如此过度刺激的货币政策下，未来6 到 12 个月内根本不可能发生经济衰退。 而去年深秋晚些时候发布的 Claude Code，让所有圈内人（对 AI 的加速爆发兴奋到了极点！ 因此我们对 AI 资本开支（CapEx）极度看多。所有这些因素叠加在一起，让我们在 1 月份全力做多股市和经济。 2、现在为什么清仓？ 虽然表层经济看起来依然强劲，但年初支持看多的所有其他指标，已经彻底来了个 180 度大反转： 1）美联储不再降息，而是在加息：我们在美联储迎来了“政权更迭，德鲁肯米勒对沃什非常熟，因为沃什曾在德鲁肯米勒家族办公室在担任合伙人多年，之前这里https://t.co/KuUFxqUCna有聊过。他知道沃什对过去 15 年我们一直搞“免费资金（零利率）”导致财政赤字和所有债务冲上云霄极其不满，对通胀连续 5 年高于目标更是深恶痛绝。 2）大宗商品见顶回落，反手做空铜。今年 1 月向上突破的大宗商品，现在看起来已经彻底见顶并掉头向下； 3）市场广度背离与信用利差走阔。1 月份还在创新高的腾落指数（Advance-Decline line），早在8 月14 日 就已经见顶了，尽管大盘指数一直撑到10月份才见顶； 4）信用利差正在不断走阔（Widening）。 在德鲁肯米勒眼里当下所有的宏观与技术指标，都跟今年 1 月份完完全全相反！ 当下他最严肃对待的 AI 看空逻辑是就是政治，以及融资问题 3、没有做多为什么也没做空？ 他现在既没有做多美股，也没有做空美股。没做空是因为AI 创新的爆发力，他说自己绝不敢去摸老虎屁股做空这里的科技创新！ 还有一点德鲁肯米勒也承认当下很多科技股近期已经严重超卖、经历了剧烈的仓位洗盘（Washed out），战术层面上机构的仓位已经降下来了。潜在意思他也认为当下做空性价比已经不高了。 但每当看不清方向的时候他自然会选择不玩了。 4、AI的下半场是什么？ 在股票市场方面，德鲁肯米勒正在全力寻找“AI 的实际应用用例”，而不是“AI 基础设施”！ AI 基础设施在经历了近期的剧烈洗盘后，或许会是一笔不错的短线战术交易（Tactical trade），但他也不认为基建硬件还能像过去四年那样，能继续充当主升浪的核心引擎。 但他认为应用层用例（Use cases）却完全有可能接棒。而且也许最有趣的“应用用例”恰恰就是前沿 AI 实验室自己！他的逻辑是：掌握全球顶级智能的实验室，没有理由继续停留在按token收费的商业模式上。 “如果你拥有世界上最强的智能，你可以开始卖任务，而不是卖token，你可以自己创建业务，”他说。 如果接下来股市还会有一波波澜壮阔的大主升浪，他认为核心就是——“卖任务，不卖 Token”。 这一点是个人很认可的，之前也有聊过https://t.co/wezCApzA2K AI主线已经迁移、中游的云厂、下游的应用都值得关注。当然从德鲁肯米勒自己的表态来看他肯定有人在关注Anthropic上市后能介入的机会。 5、对我们投资交易的启发是什么？ 1）反手的能力 看德鲁肯米勒这次讲话印象最深的一点，年初他刚刚全力做多没多久，伊朗战争爆发，他也当时慌了神砍掉了一大堆仓位； 但很很快又把仓位买回来，并且顺势把不会暴涨的杂毛股全清理干净了，让我们结结实实吃下了二季度的这波主升浪。你看发生冲击时他也会慌，也会砍仓，然后再看机会在哪里。 还有就是9月底他的机构还是高仓位运行、但现在已经清仓、明显在10月初以来的这一波调整中他夜趁机把仓位都砍掉，就是不知道他的回撤有多大。 但这种“反手”的能力值得我们学习、不让自己的判断成为执念，能随时纠正，这种灵活性是一个投资高手必须要能掌握的。 2）在棒球比赛里，有远超随机概率的“连续击球手顺期（Hitting streaks）”。 做投资也一样： 有时候站在击球区能清清楚楚看清飞过来的球，那就抡圆了胳膊下重注（Play big）； 而当感觉看不清球的时候，他就只做一点小小的触击短打（Little bunts），等什么时候胜率回升、重新看清球路了，我再重新发力。
