items.title: Gartner has cyber spending growth slowing to 11.2% next year. I think that's way too low. The outages put cyber back on everyone’s radar. The reason I think spending follows is tha
items.body: Gartner has cyber spending growth slowing to 11.2% next year. I think that's way too low. The outages put cyber back on everyone’s radar. The reason I think spending follows is that hackers are getting faster than the patch cycles companies still rely on. Anthropic is cutting its disclosure window for serious bugs from 90 days to 30 because another model can find the same flaw while the first vendor is still working on a fix. So what does the extra budget buy? Finding exposed systems earlier, testing fixes faster, and containing the flaws you can’t patch without taking something critical offline. Anne Neuberger wants AI labs helping critical infrastructure operators do exactly that. I think those labs could end up capturing a meaningful slice of the cyber budget. And honestly there is a good chance that one of the biggest cyber companies of the next decade might be an AI lab. $OSPN is one way we approached this at @AsymmetricBets_ Bets. Even if a hacker gets past the login, the bank still has to verify who approved the wire. With semis and AI infra under pressure, I still think $BUG has legs into year-end.

items.title: https://t.co/mGuJkUueVM $NVDA $MU $SNDK $LITE It is just getting started. @JensenHuang doesn't comprehend that he torched the capital of pensions and endowments whose constituents
items.body: https://t.co/mGuJkUueVM $NVDA $MU $SNDK $LITE It is just getting started. @JensenHuang doesn't comprehend that he torched the capital of pensions and endowments whose constituents depend on the money invested. Not to mention the individual savings and retirement accounts that are in the same position. ----------------------- "The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's resignation have resulted in Nvidia's stock value significantly declining. Our office is investigating whether Huang's actions have resulted in harms to Missouri's state pension funds. Missourians deserve to know those impacting their hard-earned retirement savings are not in bed with a Chinese spy." The post rides on a quoted earlier post about Huang's admission and the board's independent investigation. At my read it had about 800 impressions and 3 likes, so the room caught it essentially at publication. Why it matters: this is a new actor class in the case. Everything so far has been federal (Congress, Commerce/DOJ, the SEC probe) or private (the Kistenmacher class action). Hanaway is the first state attorney general to open a pension-harm track, which is the state-level securities and fiduciary route the Reuters liability analysis flagged on 11/11 as available but unused ("No states have brought claims"). It also fits her office's current line of work: last week she sued ISS over ESG proxy voting, framed explicitly around protecting Missouri pension returns, and the Missouri State Auditor published a report this month on the state's eight largest pension systems and their proxy voting. Whether it becomes a books-and-records demand, a Martin Act-style state investigation, or stays a press posture is the open question; the post itself announces an investigation, not a filing. ------------------------------- NVIDIA: HOW PENSIONS AND ENDOWMENTS WOULD SUE TO BE COMPENSATED Four routes, plus a fifth that costs the funds nothing. In practice a big pension runs them in sequence, not in parallel. 1. THE FEDERAL SECURITIES CLASS ACTION, AS LEAD PLAINTIFF This is the main money route. The claim is Rule 10b-5, with Section 20(a) control-person claims against Huang and the directors personally: Nvidia and Huang allegedly misled the market, the Oct 9, 2025 denial of the Megaspeed reporting being the anchor statement, and the stock's fall on the corrective disclosures (down 8.8% intraday on Nov 9, roughly $192B erased) is the loss. That case already exists: Kistenmacher v. Nvidia, filed in federal court in San Jose. Under the PSLRA, the investor with the largest financial interest in the class period (Oct 9, 2025 to Nov 8, 2026 on the current complaint) is presumptively appointed lead plaintiff, and that slot is built for institutions. MOSERS or PSRS/PEERS would file a lead-plaintiff motion by the Jan 8, 2027 deadline, take control of the case from the individual filer, pick the law firm, and negotiate the fee. Endowments do the same when their direct holdings are large enough, though most ride as class members because their Nvidia sits inside manager accounts. 2. OPTING OUT AND SUING ALONE If a fund's documented losses are big enough, it often exits the class and files its own action, 10b-5 plus state blue-sky claims (most state securities acts, Missouri's included, give a defrauded purchaser a direct damages or rescission claim). It keeps the whole recovery instead of sharing pro rata with every index holder on earth, and it controls settlement timing. Korea's National Pension Service, with an $8.9B position and a paper loss in the billions, is the profile that usually gets this pitch from the plaintiffs' bar. The tradeoff: it bears its own costs and the loss-causation fight alone. 3. DELAWARE: A SECTION 220 DEMAND, THEN A DERIVATIVE SUIT Nvidia is a Delaware corporation, so any stockholder can demand the board's books and records to investigate wrongdoing. That is the step the Reuters analysis flagged on 11/11, and it is the standard precursor. What it feeds is a derivative action in the Court of Chancery, brought in the company's name against the directors and Huang: Caremark bad-faith oversight claims (the board allegedly ignored red flags on Huang's relationships and the China exposure), breach of fiduciary duty over the denials, and clawback of Huang's compensation. The template is McDonald's, in two parts: the company clawed back about $105M from Easterbrook in 2021, and pension fund shareholders then sued the directors derivatively and settled in 2023 for about $56M, insurer-funded, plus governance reforms. Note the 8-K disclosed no severance or clawback terms for Huang, which is exactly the gap a derivative complaint attacks. Derivative recoveries go to the company, so the pension benefits as a shareholder rather than receiving a check; those settlements are funded from Side A D&O coverage. 4. THE STATE ROUTE Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced today that her office is investigating whether Huang's actions have resulted in harms to Missouri's state pension funds. An AG cannot simply collect a pension fund's trading losses. What she can do: investigate under Missouri's securities and consumer protection statutes, subpoena, and either bring an enforcement action seeking restitution and penalties or hand the pension systems a developed record to sue on. The funds themselves (MOSERS, PSRS/PEERS) remain the real plaintiffs in routes 1 to 3. Her announcement is best read as the state putting its weight, and its subpoena power, behind the funds' claims, plus political pressure on the board. 5. THE SEC FAIR FUND If the reported SEC probe matures into an enforcement action with disgorgement or penalties, Sarbanes-Oxley Section 308 lets the Commission distribute that money to harmed investors through a Fair Fund. The funds file claims rather than litigating. It is real money but historically a fraction of class-action recoveries, and it arrives on the SEC's timetable, not theirs. THE CONSTRAINTS Two constraints govern all of it. First, loss causation: defendants will argue the decline prices a sex-and-spy scandal and a CEO vacancy, not a disclosure fraud, and that the partial disclosures and the post-print recovery leave little fraud inflation to recover. The plaintiffs' counter is that the affair was the concealment mechanism, so the scandal is the fraud surfacing. Second, circularity and source: class settlements are paid mainly by Side C insurance and Nvidia's own balance sheet, which means continuing shareholders, including the suing funds, fund part of their own recovery. Huang pays personally only if a clawback or a control-person claim lands. One boundary worth noting: public pensions and endowments sit outside ERISA, so there is no separate fiduciary-breach route; ERISA plans recover the same way, as class members. Realistically the class action settles after the lead-plaintiff fight and a motion to dismiss, years out. The Section 220 demand is the only step that can move in the next few weeks, and whether a named pension files one is the first tell that this track is real.

items.title: $ANT $MU $SNDK $LITE ANTHROPIC INDEX INCLUSION: HOW THE RULES CHANGED IN 2026 2026 is the year the index industry rewired itself for the mega-IPO wave. SpaceX was the test case in
items.body: $ANT $MU $SNDK $LITE ANTHROPIC INDEX INCLUSION: HOW THE RULES CHANGED IN 2026 2026 is the year the index industry rewired itself for the mega-IPO wave. SpaceX was the test case in June, and Anthropic is the second deal through the new machinery. Every major provider except the S&P 500 now has a fast lane measured in trading days. The S&P 500 looked at the same changes, formally consulted on them, and refused. THE DEAL THE INDEXES HAVE TO DIGEST Anthropic prices tonight and trades tomorrow, Thu 11/19, on Nasdaq as ANT. 825M Class A shares at a $70 to $78 range against roughly 13.1B total shares, so a market cap of about $916B to $1.02T at the range, roughly $1.4T fully diluted, with talk of pricing above the range. The critical number for index purposes is not the trillion. It is the float: only about 6% of the shares are in the public offering. Another $26B goes in a private placement to strategic holders (Alphabet and Nvidia about $10B each, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft $1B each, TSMC $500M, per MarketWatch), and Alphabet ends up owning about 13%. Insiders are locked up 180 days with staggered early releases. The founders control 50.1% of the votes through a single share, and the S-1 itself warns the multi-class structure may make the stock ineligible for some indices. So the index question is: what does each provider do with a trillion-dollar company where only about $60B of stock actually trades? THE OLD WORLD Historically an IPO seasoned. The S&P 500 required 12 months of trading plus a profitability test. The Nasdaq-100 required three full calendar months, not counting the listing month, so a November IPO waited for the December annual reconstitution at best and usually the following year. Russell added IPOs at quarterly maintenance, typically two to five months after listing. The one exception was MSCI, which has had an early-inclusion rule for very large IPOs since 2007: meet a size test at 1.8x the segment cutoff and you can enter at the close of the tenth trading day. For two decades the system was designed to let a stock find its level, survive its lockup, and only then become forced buying for passive money. WHAT CHANGED IN 2026, PROVIDER BY PROVIDER NASDAQ-100 (EFFECTIVE MAY 1, 2026) This is the biggest change. A new Fast Entry rule: if a new listing's full market cap ranks in the top 40 of current constituents when tested at the close of its seventh trading day, Nasdaq announces the addition after the tenth trading day and adds it after the fifteenth, without removing anyone, so the index can temporarily hold more than 100 names. Two supporting changes matter as much as the headline. The 10% minimum free float, itself only introduced in June 2024, was eliminated entirely. And the weighting formula was rewritten for low-float giants: weight is based on a modified market cap equal to the price times the lesser of total shares outstanding or three times the free-float shares. A 6% float therefore gets weighted as if it were 18% of the company. Nasdaq's own FAQ worked the exact hypothetical: a $1T company floating 6% enters at about a 1% weight, and tracking funds must buy roughly $6B of stock, about 10% of the entire available float. Anthropic is that hypothetical with a ticker. There is no profitability test in the Nasdaq-100, and average daily traded value only needs to clear $5M. FTSE RUSSELL US (EFFECTIVE MAY 26, 2026) Russell added fast entry after the fifth trading day for IPOs whose investable (float-adjusted) market cap clears the Russell Top 500 breakpoint; for Anthropic the stated threshold is $17.942B of investable cap, which a $60B float clears easily. Weight is on investable cap only, no 3x multiplier, and the IPO must have at least 5% of shares public at listing or within 12 months. Russell's reconstitution is now semi-annual, June and December, which matters for the timing below. FTSE GLOBAL EQUITY INDEX SERIES Fast entry after five trading days against full-cap and investable-cap thresholds ($43.741B and $14.580B for North America). Anthropic clears both. MSCI No rule change; the 2007 framework was deemed sufficient. Early inclusion requires full market cap of at least 1.8x the interim size-segment cutoff and float-adjusted cap of at least 1.8x half the cutoff, measured at the close of the first or second trading day. Fast-track IPOs are exempt from the usual float and liquidity screens. The decision is announced no later than before the open of the third trading day, effective at the close of the tenth, unless that date falls near a scheduled review, in which case the addition is aligned with the review. S&P DOW JONES Two-tier outcome, and the split is the story. For the broad indexes (S&P Total Market, S&P Completion, Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market), S&P added a fast track effective June 8, 2026: an IPO qualifies with an investable weight factor of at least 0.10, or a float-adjusted cap of at least 10% of the 100th-largest company in the index, with five business days' notice and no profitability or seasoning requirement. For the S&P 500, MidCap 400 and SmallCap 600, S&P ran a formal consultation (opened April 30, closed May 28) proposing exactly what Nasdaq did: cut seasoning to six months and waive profitability and float minimums for megacaps. On June 4 it rejected its own proposal in full. The 12-month seasoning stays, the 10% float minimum stays, and the GAAP profitability test stays: positive net income from continuing operations in the most recent quarter and across the trailing four quarters combined. S&P said explicitly that exceptions should not be granted solely based on market capitalization. Reporting since (including a June letter from Senator Warren) says SpaceX lobbied the providers hard for these changes; Nasdaq and Russell moved, S&P did not. CRSP AND MORNINGSTAR Total-market indexes also fast-track at about five trading days, which is why total-market funds pick Anthropic up by the end of November. ANTHROPIC'S ACTUAL INCLUSION CALENDAR First trade Thu 11/19. Counting trading days around Thanksgiving (closed Thu 11/26): • MSCI is first. The decision must be announced by Mon 11/23, before the open of the third trading day. The tenth trading day is Thu 12/3, but because that falls right against the November index review, MSCI's alignment rule points to effectiveness at the close of Mon 11/30, with the November review. Either way, MSCI money is in within the first eight trading days. • CRSP and Morningstar total market: roughly five trading days, so by the end of November. • Russell US: the five-day rule would have landed the addition on Wed 11/25, but FTSE Russell's November 13 notices said the Thanksgiving collision pushes Anthropic into the December semi-annual reconstitution instead: added after the close Fri 12/11, effective at the open Mon 12/14. • Nasdaq-100: the seventh-day test is the close of Mon 11/30, and at anything near a $1T cap Anthropic is comfortably top 40 (the cutoff is roughly $100B). The fifteenth trading day is Thu 12/10, but Nasdaq is folding the addition into its mid-December annual reconstitution and rebalancing rather than trading twice, so the effective entry is the December reconstitution, before the open Mon 12/21, at roughly a 1% weight on the 3x-float formula. FTSE Global lands the same morning, effective Mon 12/21 after the close Fri 12/18. • S&P 500: nothing. Twelve months of seasoning means November 2027 at the earliest, and the profitability gate is the binding constraint regardless: Anthropic is GAAP loss-making, so it needs four consecutive profitable quarters summed positive plus a positive latest quarter before the committee can even consider it, then committee discretion on top. Realistically 2028. The S&P Total Market fast track, by contrast, can hold it within days, so an investor in a total-market fund owns Anthropic almost immediately while an S&P 500 fund holder owns none of it. That divergence between the two most common fund types is new, and it is a direct product of the June split. THE FLOW MATH AND WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE TAPE Intropic estimates total passive demand across all the indexes adding Anthropic at roughly $19B (estimate, via MarketWatch). Set that against a public float of about $60B: index trackers need to own on the order of a third of the tradable supply within the first month, in three dated cliffs, 11/30 (MSCI), 12/14 (Russell) and 12/21 (Nasdaq-100 and FTSE Global). That is a structural, price-insensitive bid under the aftermarket, and it interacts with the allocation dynamics in the deal: most funds were zeroed or filled at a fraction of their orders, so the aftermarket has both disappointed active money and forced passive money chasing the same 6% float. It is also the mirror image of the funding drain: the passive complex that effectively funded allocations becomes a scheduled buyer of ANT through December, while the offsetting sale inside the Nasdaq-100 is spread pro rata across all constituents at about 1% of each weight, a trim, not a hit, to names like Nvidia (6.52% of QQQ as of 11/13). The SpaceX precedent is the cautionary data point. SPCX listed June 12, entered the Nasdaq-100 before the open July 7 at a weight below 1%, and fell about 15% over its first stretch in the index. Fast inclusion does not guarantee aftermarket performance; it guarantees flow, and flow into a 6% float cuts both ways when the lockup calendar starts releasing shares and weights get reset at the quarterly rebalances. The staggered lockup releases through the first half of 2027 will raise Anthropic's float, and every float step-up mechanically raises its Russell and MSCI weights (which use float-adjusted cap) at the next review, creating a series of smaller, pre-announced passive bids into mid-2027, with the June 2027 Russell reconstitution the largest. The genuinely big event remains the S&P 500, because that is where the deepest passive pool sits, and on current rules it cannot happen before late 2027 and only after profitability. If Anthropic's GAAP numbers inflect the way its revenue has ($33.2B in 2026 per its filing, still with an operating loss), the S&P 500 add becomes the 2028 flow story, telegraphed a year in advance. One governance footnote worth knowing: the index industry just spent 2026 proving it will rewrite rules for size, and S&P's refusal is now the outlier position under commercial pressure. If the S&P committee ever revisits the June decision, Anthropic and SpaceX are the two names that force the question, and a rule change there would be the single largest passive flow event of the cycle.

items.title: Multi-agent systems often behave like a mob, not like a coordinated team. We are releasing Multi Agent Coordination Bench: a benchmark requiring agent coordination, collaboration a
items.body: Multi-agent systems often behave like a mob, not like a coordinated team. We are releasing Multi Agent Coordination Bench: a benchmark requiring agent coordination, collaboration and communication. Right now, agents benefit from parallel exploration, but their coordination and communication is very poor. A team of eight agents does better than a single agent but often due to random exploration, while their coordination has significant room for improvement. Our tasks include agent teams trying to execute a mission to Mars, fight zombies, grow a company from seed, and more. We categorize our tasks by two properties of the environment: if the agents share the same information and actions (Shared vs Distributed), and if they pursue the same goal or not (Collaborative/Strategic). This taxonomy will be useful for future research, to think about different multi-agentic problems across distributed and strategic settings.

external_articles.title: Nokia powers CMC Networks’ EMEA-R corridor, connecting key hubs across Europe, the Middle East and Africa
external_articles.body:
Nokia announced today that its optical networking technology is enabling CMC Networks to expand high-capacity international connectivity across Africa, the Middle East and Europe through its new Europe-Middle East-Africa Ring (EMEA-R). Connecting six strategic network nodes across the three regions, EMEA-R delivers scalable, carrier-grade connectivity to help wholesale and enterprise customers expand into new markets with greater flexibility and resilience.

EMEA-R provides reliable International Private Leased Circuit (IPLC) connectivity with dedicated 1G, 10G and 100G capacity. Through a single contract, SLA and operational relationship with CMC Networks, customers can simplify the management of their international connectivity. Pre-built, pre-lit capacity across established routes also enables faster service activation, helping customers expand into new markets with greater flexibility and resilience.

EMEA-R demonstrates how advanced optical transport infrastructure can help address the growing demand for seamless, high-performance connectivity across markets. By combining Nokia’s optical technology with CMC Networks’ regional reach and service expertise, the corridor gives wholesale and enterprise customers greater flexibility in how they access and scale international capacity. It also strengthens the connectivity foundation needed to support the evolution of cloud, AI and digital services across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

With EMEA-R, we are addressing a key need among carriers and enterprises for reliable, flexible and scalable connectivity across international markets. By combining our regional expertise and network reach with Nokia’s optical transport technology, we are simplifying how customers access and manage capacity across Africa, the Middle East and Europe. This enables them to scale with greater confidence, while supporting the growing demand for connectivity driven by cloud, AI and digital transformation.

EMEA-R combines terrestrial and subsea infrastructure, with the first phase connecting Johannesburg to London via Cape Town and the Atlantic, and Jeddah to Marseille via the Red Sea and Mediterranean. High-performance terrestrial routes link London, Frankfurt and Marseille. The corridor is supported by flexible, carrier-grade optical technology from Nokia, powered by the 1830 Photonic Service Switch platform, with extensions to data centers, internet exchanges, customer sites and onward regional destinations available on request.

EMEA-R reinforces the importance of regional connectivity in supporting Africa’s digital economy. As AI, cloud and data-intensive applications drive demand for high-capacity, reliable networks, the corridor strengthens connectivity between Africa, the Middle East and Europe, helping businesses scale their operations, access digital infrastructure and tap into emerging opportunities across the region.

The corridor is designed to evolve alongside customer needs, with future expansion plans expected to further strengthen connectivity between Africa, the Middle East and Europe. The corridor is designed to evolve alongside customer needs, supporting future service enhancements and network expansion across the region.

Nokia is a global leader in connectivity infrastructure, enabling the AI supercycle. We build networks that connect intelligence and deliver a comprehensive connectivity solution across fixed, mobile, IP, optical, core, and data center networks. With security by design, AI-driven innovation, and AI-optimized architecture, Nokia delivers trusted infrastructure that enables AI to scale and advances connectivity to secure a brighter world.

external_articles.title: Oasis Networks Selects PacketLight for Burstable Wavelength Services
external_articles.body:
LISBON, November 17, 2026 – PacketLight Networks, a provider of DWDM and OTN optical transport solutions, today announced that Oasis Networks has selected its 800G transport and OLS optical amplification platforms to support the development of burstable wavelength services in Portugal. PacketLight’s open transport architecture supports Oasis’ plans to allocate optical capacity through software as customer requirements change.

The connection between Lisbon and Sines is now in place, with the Sines endpoint at Start Campus. A proof of concept on Oasis’ operational network demonstrated software-controlled optical path establishment and reconfiguration. PacketLight has also completed the design for future site interconnects around the Lisbon metro ring.

Oasis’ service design pairs an always-on 100G base connection with additional 100G and 400G capacity on demand and 800G capacity for scheduled requirements. It targets large data transfers, backup and replication windows, and connectivity for cloud and emerging distributed AI workloads. The aim is to align customers’ bandwidth commitments more closely with actual demand while making better use of Oasis’ available transport resources.

“Their team responded quickly and worked through the design with us, including the future ring interconnects. It allowed us to invest in what we needed to get started, with a clear plan and budget for our next expansion,” said Andre Folgado, Co-founder of Oasis Networks.

PacketLight supplies PL-8000M muxponders and PL-1000IL/GIL EDFA optical amplifiers for the backbone. The PL-8000M supports 100GbE, 400GbE and 800GbE services over two 800G DWDM wavelengths, delivering up to 1.6 Tbps per platform. The amplifiers compensate for optical loss along the fiber routes, supporting the links between sites.

On the client side, iPronics ONE-32 optical circuit switches connect customer-facing ports to available transport resources, while Oasis controls their allocation. PacketLight’s open architecture allows Oasis to combine these technologies within its own network design. Management interfaces, including REST APIs, provide integration options as Oasis develops its controller to coordinate switching and transport.

PacketLight’s stackable, disaggregated platforms also support phased investment as Oasis adds sites and capacity. High-capacity aggregation helps Oasis make more use of its existing fiber, while the absence of feature-activation licensing fees supports predictable ownership costs. The completed ring interconnect design gives Oasis a defined plan for its next expansion.

“Oasis wanted the freedom to develop new optical services while owning and controlling its network,” said Michal Naor, VP Business Development at PacketLight Networks. “We worked with its team to support the 100G, 400G and 800G service model and design the next network interconnects. Our open transport architecture gives Oasis the flexibility to integrate its chosen switching technology and expand capacity in stages as demand grows.”

For 26 years, PacketLight Networks has delivered optical transport solutions to telecommunications carriers, data center operators, cloud providers and enterprises. Its DWDM and OTN portfolio supports high-capacity connectivity, OLS optical amplification and Layer-1 encryption, with open architectures that help customers expand their networks and integrate technologies from multiple vendors. For more information, visit www.packetlight.com .

Oasis Networks is a next-generation telecommunications operator building the autonomous optical and IP network for the AI era. Engineered to serve high-capacity workloads globally, Oasis operates a software-defined photonic fabric providing on-demand Layer 1 optical transport, carrier-grade IP transit, and metrology-grade precision timing. With native post-quantum cryptography and automated API-driven provisioning, Oasis interconnects premier carrier-neutral data centers, AI gigawatt campuses, and global subsea cable landings with the physical reach of a telecom backbone and the elasticity of cloud infrastructure.

external_articles.title: Scintil Photonics Wins Best Business Strategy at the 2026 IPC Start-Up Competition | 24/7 Business Reporter
external_articles.body:
GRENOBLE, France, Nov.  18, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Scintil Photonics, developer of LEAF Light™, a single-chip dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) laser source for high-density optical connectivity in scale-up networks, today announced that it has won Best Business Strategy in the Start-Up Competition, co-organized by the IEEE Photonics Society and LightCounting, at the 2026 IEEE Photonics Conference (IPC). Scintil designs LEAF Light™ for the optical links between GPUs in AI clusters, and a commercial foundry manufactures it. Scintil enters the market through a multi-source standard laser module and times its ramp to customers' need to scale up their GPU systems across multiple racks and move from copper to optics.

"In AI data centers, manufacturing will decide the winners, not architecture demos," said Matt Crowley, CEO of Scintil Photonics. "The open question is whether multi-wavelength laser sources can be made at hyperscale volume and yield. Our strategy rests on how LEAF Light™ is made: in a silicon photonics wafer process, rather than assembled from parts."

Scintil is a fabless semiconductor company: it designs both the chips and the process. Scintil put its engineering into SHIP™ (Scintil Heterogeneous Integrated Photonics), which adds laser steps to the existing silicon photonics flow of a foundry such as Tower Semiconductor , instead of developing an entirely new process. The process bonds indium phosphide dies onto the backside of a finished silicon photonics wafer and forms the lasers with standard etching; the rest of the foundry's flow runs unchanged. SHIP™ is validated on Tower's silicon photonics production lines. Tower runs the same lines in mass production for optical transceivers.

In designs built from discrete indium phosphide lasers, each aligned and packaged on its own, every added wavelength means another laser, another alignment, another lens, and another monitoring diode. In LEAF Light™, the laser array, multiplexer, monitoring photodiodes, and frequency reference are fabricated together on one chip, and lithography sets each wavelength, which is checked at wafer level. The cost of a wavelength becomes a lithography cost that does not grow with channel count.

Scintil starts with the Optical Compute Interconnect Multi-Source Agreement (OCI MSA) ELSFP, a pluggable laser module. The module feeds light to the customer's co-packaged optics (CPO) or near-packaged optics (NPO) engine, which does the modulation and detection. Customers can multi-source their ELSFP, and adding Scintil as a supplier reduces supply-chain risk during shortages. Because LEAF Light™ multiplexes its wavelengths on the chip, the number of laser-source fibers stays the same as a design adds wavelengths, so customers can add channels without redrawing their fiber routing.

Within the standard, Scintil competes on simpler packaging and on telemetry. A single LEAF Light™ chip lets module assemblers use lens arrays, simplifying fiber alignment. With Scintil's companion control chip, LEAF Light™ is designed to report output power, temperature, and wavelength spacing continuously, so system providers and hyperscalers can monitor their laser sources across a data center as a fleet.

AI clusters now span racks. Their scale-up links are still copper, and copper runs out of reach, density, and bandwidth at cluster scale. The industry is moving toward CPO and NPO designs that carry many wavelengths on each fiber. Scintil aligns its production schedule with the rollout of GPU systems built on DWDM optical interconnects at hyperscalers.

SHIP™ can also integrate semiconductor optical amplifiers and high-speed modulators in the same flow as the lasers, and Scintil plans to use the process in designs that need III-V (compound semiconductor) material integrated with silicon photonics at foundry volume, extending Scintil's addressable market beyond laser sources.

Scintil closed a $58 million (€50 million) Series B in September 2025, led by Yotta Capital Partners and NGP Capital, with participation from NVIDIA. LEAF Light™ has been sampled to customers. Field trials are planned for 2027 and first volume production for 2028. The LEAF Light™ Evaluation Kit is available through Scintil's early access program, and interested organizations can request access at https://www.scintil-photonics.com/evkleaflight .

Scintil Photonics is the global leader in DWDM laser sources for AI. Using its SHIP™ (Scintil Heterogeneous Integrated Photonics) technology, Scintil developed LEAF Light™, the world's first single-chip DWDM laser source for high-density optical connectivity in scale-up networks. LEAF Light™ enables hyperscalers to meet the power, tail latency, utilization, and bandwidth demands of large-scale GPU clusters, leveraging next-generation co-packaged optics (CPO). Headquartered in Grenoble, France, with operations across North America, Scintil is built to support global needs for advanced AI infrastructure.

external_articles.title: China's Eoptolink denies optical module order-cut rumors: 1.6T in mass volume production, order backlog ample — BigGo Finance
external_articles.body:
Eoptolink Technology (300502.SZ) on November 18 released an announcement on its production and operations, offering a direct response to market concerns about demand. The company stated clearly that customer demand guidance for optical modules is clear, its order backlog is ample, and there is no downward revision of demand expectations or order cancellation, adding that it holds a positive outlook for order demand growth in the fourth quarter of this year and next year.

The statement comes as demand for high-speed optical interconnect continues to climb worldwide amid the ongoing buildout of artificial intelligence computing infrastructure, placing the optical module industry at a critical stage of product iteration and industrial upgrading. The market had previously been divided over the pace of downstream customers' capital expenditure, and Eoptolink's announcement amounts to an official position on those concerns.

On the product front, 800G and 1.6T optical modules form the company's main product lineup this year, with 1.6T optical modules already in mass volume production. Commercialization of next-generation products is also advancing steadily: development of NPO products is progressing smoothly, with volume shipments expected in 2027 and large-scale delivery in 2028; in areas such as CPO and OCS, the company has completed technical groundwork and product positioning.

On capacity, both the Chengdu and Thailand production bases are rapidly expanding capacity to meet delivery requirements from continued order growth. The company said that as expansion proceeds, its product delivery capability will be further enhanced, positioning it well for the next phase of product demand.

Note: The above information comes from the company's November 18 announcement on its recent production and operations.

A buyback update disclosed the same day showed that under the share buyback plan announced on October 23, 2026, the repurchase size is no less than CNY 800 million and no more than CNY 1 billion. As of November 18, the company had repurchased a cumulative 4,216,253 shares through its dedicated securities account for share buybacks via centralized bidding, representing 0.3023% of total share capital, at a maximum price of 213.27 yuan per share and a minimum price of 172.05 yuan per share, for a total transaction amount of about CNY 799.86 million (approximately $120.2 million), excluding transaction fees.

From an industry perspective, optical module demand is closely tied to the pace of artificial intelligence data center construction, and the speed at which high-speed products ramp up directly determines the revenue elasticity of the companies involved. Eoptolink's emphasis at this point on ample orders and the 1.6T ramp-up helps ease market worries that demand for the optical module sector has peaked, while its groundwork in next-generation technology routes such as NPO and CPO bears on the company's competitive position over a longer cycle. The buyback amount has approached the lower limit of the plan, also signaling to some extent management's view of the current valuation. Variables to watch going forward include the actual pace of overseas customers' capital expenditure and whether expansion at the Chengdu and Thailand bases can keep pace with delivery schedules.

external_articles.title: Chinese optics module leader proposes RMB 2–4 billion share repurchase | KuCoin
external_articles.body:
The chairman of the leading optical module company proposes repurchasing RMB 2 billion to 4 billion; 37.49 billion yuan in large orders for computing power-related stocks explicitly adopt compliant servers within China; the leading paper manufacturer to suspend trading starting tomorrow... What notable announcements should you watch for after today’s market close?

On November 18, the chairman of Zhongji Xuchuang proposed repurchasing shares worth RMB 2 billion to RMB 4 billion; all servers to be deployed under the RMB 37.49 billion computing power cloud service agreement with Xiechuang Data are compliant domestic servers; Shanying International will suspend trading effective November 19 due to planned significant matters.

Here are the selected after-hours announcements:

Zhongji旭创 announces that Chairman and CEO Liu Sheng has proposed that the company repurchase its A-shares using its own or self-raised funds through centralized bidding transactions, with a total repurchase amount of no less than RMB 2 billion and no more than RMB 4 billion. The repurchase price shall not exceed 150% of the average trading price of the stock over the 30 trading days prior to the board’s approval of the repurchase plan. The repurchased shares will be used for equity incentives or employee stock ownership plans, as well as to maintain the company’s value and shareholder interests.

Co-create Data announces that, in October 2026, its wholly-owned subsidiary, Co-create Intelligent Computing Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., signed a cloud computing services agreement with a client company, with an expected total value not exceeding RMB 37.49 billion. The agreement has officially taken effect. As of the date of this announcement, the company has issued formal purchase orders for the corresponding server equipment to qualified suppliers, and the suppliers have confirmed in writing their production scheduling and delivery timelines. After verification, all servers to be deployed under this agreement are compliant domestic servers. These servers do not involve using overseas cloud computing resources as the source of performance for this project.

Shanying International announced that it has been notified by relevant parties that they are planning a significant matter involving the company. Given the substantial uncertainty surrounding this matter, and upon application to the Shanghai Stock Exchange, the company’s A-shares will be suspended from trading beginning at the open on November 19, 2026, with an expected suspension period of no more than two trading days. During the suspension, the company will fulfill its information disclosure obligations based on the progress of the matter. This significant matter is still in the planning stage, with the specific plan under discussion and deliberation, and its implementation remains highly uncertain. Investors are hereby advised to exercise caution and be aware of the associated investment risks.

Luyan Pharmaceutical announced that its seventh board of directors held its first meeting on November 18, 2026, electing Wu Di as Chairman of the Board and appointing him as General Manager; Wu Di also became the company’s legal representative. The meeting also elected Wu Jinxiang as Vice Chairman and appointed other executives, including Deputy General Managers, Chief Financial Officer, and Secretary of the Board, whose terms will expire upon the conclusion of the current board’s term.

Kanghong Pharmaceutical has announced that its subsidiary, Chengdu Kanghong Biotechnology Co., Ltd., received a notice from the National Medical Products Administration approving the clinical trial of KHN923 Injection. This drug is a Category 1 therapeutic biological product indicated for Alzheimer’s disease and is a bispecific antibody targeting beta-amyloid and transferrin receptor 1.

Sunshine Holdings announced that it plans to repurchase its shares for a total amount of RMB 50 million (inclusive) to RMB 100 million (inclusive), at a price not exceeding RMB 9.12 per share (inclusive). The repurchased shares will be used for equity incentives or employee stock ownership plans. Based on the upper and lower limits of the repurchase funding and the maximum repurchase price, the estimated number of shares to be repurchased is approximately 5.4825 million to 10.9649 million shares, representing about 0.73% to 1.46% of the company's total outstanding shares.

澜起科技 announces the completion of its second A-share repurchase program for 2026. The program aimed to repurchase shares with a budget of RMB 300 million to RMB 500 million, at a maximum price of RMB 280 per share, with the repurchased shares intended for use in employee stock ownership plans or equity incentives. As of November 18, 2026, the company had cumulatively repurchased 3.3139 million A-shares, representing 0.27% of its total share capital, at a highest price of RMB 169.94 per share, a lowest price of RMB 128.58 per share, an average price of RMB 150.88 per share, and a total repurchase amount of approximately RMB 500 million (excluding transaction fees such as commissions and transfer charges). The actual execution of this repurchase aligns exactly with the originally disclosed plan.

Huatai Securities announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Pioneer Reward Limited, has increased the principal amount of its offshore medium-term note program from $3 billion (equivalent) to $10 billion (equivalent). The company has recently applied to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange for an updated listing of this note program. Within 12 months following the effective date of this updated listing, the notes will be issued solely to professional investors as defined by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, through debt offerings. The effective date of this updated listing is expected to be November 19, 2026.

Xingfa Group announces that the company plans to jointly establish a controlling subsidiary, Yuan'an Xinghuahui Mining Co., Ltd., with Tongling Wanqiao Mining Co., Ltd., with a registered capital of RMB 4 billion. Xingfa Group will contribute RMB 2.04 billion in cash, accounting for 51% of the equity, while Tongling Wanqiao will contribute RMB 1.96 billion, accounting for 49%. The subsidiary will primarily focus on acquiring and developing phosphate ore rights and expanding into downstream phosphorus chemical products such as phosphoric acid.

Shenghong Technology announced that on November 17, 2026, it received a Loan Commitment Letter from Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Huizhou Branch, committing to provide a dedicated loan facility of up to RMB 270 million for the company’s share repurchase, not exceeding 90% of the total repurchase amount, with a loan term of no more than three years. Previously, the company intended to repurchase shares using its own funds or raised funds ranging from RMB 150 million to RMB 300 million, at a price not exceeding RMB 240.49 per share.

Megmeet announced its intention to repurchase its issued RMB ordinary shares (A-shares) through centralized bidding transactions, with a total repurchase amount of no less than RMB 200 million and no more than RMB 400 million, and a repurchase price not exceeding RMB 128 per share. The repurchased shares will be used for equity incentives or employee stock ownership plans.

Tianfu Communications announced that, in terms of new technology deployment, the company continues to advance research and development in cutting-edge technologies such as CPO, NPO, and silicon photonics. CPO-related products have entered mass delivery phase, with clear customer demand; the company expects volume growth for these products to gradually increase starting in 2027. NPO-related products are currently in the stages of R&D advancement, customer sampling, and validation, with overall progress on track. If subsequent validation and customer adoption proceed smoothly, large-scale production is expected to gradually begin in 2027. The company will continue to strengthen collaboration in frontier technology R&D and actively promote the commercialization of new technologies.

Tianfu Communications announced that, as of November 18, 2026, the company had cumulatively repurchased 880,000 shares through its dedicated securities account for share repurchases via centralized bidding transactions, representing 0.0807% of the company’s current total share capital. The highest transaction price was RMB 150 per share, the lowest was RMB 103.17 per share, and the total transaction amount was RMB 108 million (excluding transaction fees).

Yamadon announced that its controlling shareholder, Yamadon Technology (Yancheng) Co., Ltd., has entered into a Share Transfer Agreement with Shanghai Qixing Network Technology Co., Ltd. Upon completion of this transaction, control of the company will change. However, the company’s core business will remain unchanged. The company’s primary business continues to be the deep processing of photovoltaic glass, with no significant changes. The transferee and its actual controller have also committed that, for 36 months following the completion of the share transfer registration, they will not inject any assets they or their affiliates hold into the listed company and have no plans to do so.

Leo Co., Ltd. announced that Wang Xiangrong, the controlling shareholder, actual controller, chairman, and general manager, based on his confidence in the company’s future development and recognition of its intrinsic value, has proposed that the company use its own funds or raised funds to repurchase a portion of its shares through centralized bidding, with the repurchased shares to be canceled and the company’s registered capital reduced accordingly. The proposed total repurchase amount is no less than RMB 50 million (inclusive) and no more than RMB 100 million (inclusive).

Sino-Optics has issued an announcement regarding its recent production and operational status. Customer demand guidance for optical modules remains clear, with a robust order backlog and no indications of downward revisions or order cancellations. The company maintains a positive outlook for order growth in the fourth quarter of this year and into next year. On the production front, both the Chengdu and Thailand manufacturing facilities are rapidly scaling up capacity to meet growing order delivery demands. The 800G and 1.6T optical modules are the company’s key products this year, with the 1.6T optical modules now entering a phase of large-scale volume production.

Xinyisheng announced that on October 23, 2026, the company disclosed a share repurchase plan with a funding amount of no less than RMB 800 million and no more than RMB 1 billion. As of November 18, 2026, the company had repurchased 4.2163 million shares through its dedicated securities account for share repurchases via centralized bidding transactions, representing 0.3023% of the company’s total shares outstanding. The highest transaction price was RMB 213.27 per share, the lowest was RMB 172.05 per share, and the total transaction amount reached RMB 800 million (excluding transaction fees). items.body: $Tencent / Chinese CSPs’ tone on the AI capex cycle is very clear - Martin Lau laid out a clear case for why AI capex should moderate after 2027: 1/ Front-loaded investment: AI infrastructure is like building a factory. Once built, it can continuously train new models and generate tokens. 2/ Lower hardware costs: The same equipment should cost significantly less by 2028. 3/ Rapid efficiency gains: The same infrastructure can deliver exponentially more training compute and token output over time. Takeaway: Martin is effectively calling for a peak in AI capex in 2026-27, with a meaningful decline in capex intensity thereafter, even as AI demand continues to grow. The read-through for semis is interesting: If annual industry AI capex eventually normalizes below $1T, assigning a mid-range multiple to normalized earnings, that’s your industry total size.

items.title: Jon Gray, President & COO of Blackstone $BX, at TomorrowX Summit. Another fascinating discussion about the AI bubble. Gray believes the skepticism has become excessively negative.
items.body: Jon Gray, President & COO of Blackstone $BX, at TomorrowX Summit. Another fascinating discussion about the AI bubble. Gray believes the skepticism has become excessively negative. During the 1990s telecom bubble, companies laid massive amounts of fiber and waited for demand to arrive. AI today is different. Demand is already surging, while chips, power, and data center capacity struggle to keep up. Unlike the 2008 housing bubble, much of today's AI investment is being driven by cash-generating companies rather than excessive leverage. Blackstone is focusing on the bottlenecks: natural gas, power plants, electrical equipment, and data centers. Gray also sees opportunities in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and healthcare. Perhaps the real question isn't how much capital is being spent on AI. It's whether demand exists, who is financing the buildout, and where the actual constraints are.

external_articles.title: The Earthshot Prize Unveils Game Changing Partnerships at Impact Assembly - The Earthshot Prize
external_articles.body:
Hundreds of millions of people around the world will breathe cleaner air, be better protected from extreme weather and benefit from healthier oceans and a more stable climate, as The Earthshot Prize unveils a wave of major breakthroughs to scale environmental solutions.

Amazon, NVIDIA, Uber and IKEA are among the global names joining forces with Earthshot Prize Winners and Finalists, as new partnerships, investments and expansions were announced at the Prize’s Impact Assembly in Mumbai.

Spanning continents and sectors, the milestones will help transform entire systems. They will bring cleaner air to more than 200 million people in India and dramatically scale up protection from extreme weather for 100 million smallholder farmers. They will also include new long-term funding to protect our oceans, and stronger protection from extreme heat for more than 100,000 women in low-income communities across South Asia.

The Impact Assembly will bring together environmental innovators, business leaders, philanthropists and government representatives, turning ambition to repair our planet into action.

2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Pula (Fix Our Climate) has announced it has secured new partnerships with two of the world’s leading technology companies, putting it on course to quadruple the number of smallholder farmers it protects from extreme weather to 100 million by 2030.

Amazon will announce a commitment to cover the full cost of Pula’s cloud credits through to 2030. It will also give Pula new climate data, technical expertise and access to its vast partner network, which will strengthen the platform as it grows.

Pula also unveiled that it is joining the NVIDIA Inception programme, which gives startups access to cutting-edge technology, training and connections with the venture capital ecosystem. Through the programme, Pula will use NVIDIA Earth-2 , an AI platform for weather and climate. It produces far more detailed forecasts than traditional models and does so at much greater speed. With Earth-2’s advanced modelling, Pula will be able to see more clearly how drought and extreme weather will affect the farmers it serves.

2025 Earthshot Prize Finalist the State of Gujarat (Clean Our Air), which pioneered the world’s first trading scheme to cut harmful particle pollution from factories, will, through its partner the Emissions Market Accelerator , expand its model to more Indian states, potentially benefiting a further 210 million people.

The scale-ups, first in Maharashtra and followed by work in Rajasthan, let industry grow while giving people cleaner, healthier air to breathe. The scheme sets a limit on how much pollution factories can release in total. Factories that cut their pollution can sell their unused allowance to others, which rewards businesses for cleaning up.

2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Mahindra Last Mile Mobility (Clean Our Air) announced a partnership with Uber to speed up India’s switch to electric rickshaws, one of the world’s most significant green transitions. Mahindra’s electric three-wheelers will join Uber’s platform, and incentives will help drivers in some of the world’s most polluted cities trade in older, polluting vehicles for clean ones.

2025 Finalist Matter (Revive Our Oceans) announced its first solution designed to capture microfibres from wastewater at an IKEA textile supplier in India. Microfibres released during textile production are a shared challenge for the textile industry and addressing them requires practical solutions that work in real factory environments.

Through Inter IKEA’s investment in Matter, the organisations are supporting the development of technology designed to capture microfibres from wastewater. This first installation at an IKEA textile supplier in India is an important opportunity to learn from its performance in an industrial setting and explore its potential for wider use.

2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Satellites on Fire (Clean Our Air) has revealed an expansion of its AI-powered wildfire detection to Brazil and Panama. Ahead of El Niño season, it will monitor 7.4 million hectares in Panama, nearly the entire country, for the first time.

The Argentinian company will also protect 135,000 hectares of the Peruvian Amazon. In Brazil, it has signed a two-year agreement with leading global agribusiness Bunge, its first commercial deployment in the country.

2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Mother Earth Foundation (Build a Waste-Free World) has announced it is bringing its community- led waste schemes to six more cities and provinces in the Philippines. The expansion will benefit more than 2 million people and keep over 250,000 tonnes of waste a year out of landfill. It will also support the livelihoods of nearly 5,000 informal waste workers.

2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Mahila Housing Trust (Fix Our Climate) has announced they are protecting a further 100,000 women in low-income communities across Asia from extreme heat, and a world-first insurance scheme for pregnant women.

With the NGO HERA , the Trust announced HERA Materna in India, the first insurance scheme to protect pregnant women against extreme heat. It pays at lower temperatures than standard policies, and philanthropic funding tops up the payouts so expectant mothers can afford to rest on the hottest days. Throughout pregnancy, women also get access to cooling, medical care, heatwave warnings and health advice.

The Trust has also announced new heat insurance to Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Philippines, where it will support 60,000 women by the end of 2027. In India, it is moving into Nabha in Punjab and Bikaner in Rajasthan. There it will help local governments plan for extreme heat and install 50,000 cool roofs, coated with reflective paint that keeps homes up to five degrees cooler.

2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Niue Ocean Wide Trust (Revive Our Oceans) has announced it has secured a new US$2.7 million commitment from the Global Environment Facility , one of the world’s largest backers of environmental action. The investment makes Niue one of the few Trusts to unite five sources of finance: individuals, businesses, foundations, governments and a multilateral fund.

2021 Earthshot Prize Finalist SOLshare (Fix Our Climate) has announced it has signed US$20 million in new solar energy deals through its Greener Garments Initiative . The contracts will deliver more than 45 megawatts of solar power to two Bangladeshi garment manufacturers that supply global fashion brands. They will also power Chittagong Port, the gateway for most of the country’s clothing exports. The climate benefit equals planting more than 160,000 trees every year for 20 years.

As the world’s second-largest clothing exporter, Bangladesh is key to helping global fashion brands hit their climate targets.

2022 Earthshot Prize Finalist Phool (Build a Waste-Free World) has revealed a US$6 million in new debt financing from three major Indian banks: the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim), the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) and ICICI Bank. The deal shows that circular-economy solutions are winning the backing of mainstream finance.

Phool turns temple flowers that would otherwise be dumped in rivers and landfill into a leather alternative that is free of animal products and plastic. Since 2022, it has grown from processing 36 tonnes of flowers a day in two Indian states to 50 tonnes a day across four.

Together, these major breakthroughs show how investment, partnerships and expansions are helping proven environmental solutions reach more people and places around the world and change entire systems for the better.

items.title: 673: Nvidia Without Jensen Huang, GPT-6.2 Backlash, Two Questions for Anthropic’s IPO, OpenAI + NATO, a Sky Full of Satellites, Dyson’s $10 Fix, and Lord of the Rings
items.body: Passing one obstacle simply says you’re worthy of more. —Ryan Holiday 🛰️🌐 This is going on above your head at all times. Photographer Brendan Larsen created this amazing composite: This is the most time-consuming photo edit I’ve EVER done! I left my camera photographing the night sky over Mt Taranaki for nearly TWO HOURS, capturing 578 photographs. The result? An estimated 14,450 satellite trail appearances, representing approximately 1,400 individual satellites! 😱 I manually masked in EVERY SINGLE TRAIL from the original photographs — approximately 45 HOURS of editing to create this one image! h/t Friend-of-the-show and supporter DvorakQ (💚 🥃) on the private discord! ⚙️🛠️🧰 Pro-tip for you: If you have a Dyson cordless vacuum, maybe because you bought one after hearing David Senra’s (🎙️📚) episode about James Dyson in 2021, and you’ve had it for a number of years, buy a new one of these: You can get non-Dyson ones on Amazon for less than half the price of the original one. Maybe I didn’t read the instructions closely enough, but I thought these filters just needed to be washed with water once in a while. Turns out, they are consumable 😅 My V15 was starting to have problems. I suspected the hardwood brush (the yellow and blue one that spins), because when I plugged it in, I got the “airways blocked” warning, but I didn’t get it with other attachments. I was about to spend 150 CAD on a new brush, but on a hunch, I decided to order a new filter. Holy! It’s like I got a brand new vacuum. It sucks so much — in a good way 😅 — that I feel it pulling against carpets and floorboards in a way that I haven’t felt in years. Performance had been degrading so gradually that I never noticed the problem. I’m glad I spent ~10 CAD on a filter rather than more on an attachment that wouldn’t have solved the problem, and then maybe I would’ve just bought a whole new V15 for a thousand bucks. I figure this is a good enough tip to share with you. 💚 🥃 To keep this steamboat alive and afloat , I need supporters. Like you ! 🚢 The paid subscription includes the full feed, every podcast, Zoom Q&As with me, and access to the private Discord clubhouse , where a core group of us hang out and discuss the interesting stuff we find: Get the full Liberty feed and help keep the Serendipity Engine running by becoming a paid supporter. Thank you 💚🥃🦊🐙⚓️ 🏦 💰 Liberty Capital 💳 💴 🏎️ Fall From Grace: The World Changed Faster Than Jensen Did 🪽 I have written and rewritten thousands of words on this since last week. Events happened so fast that right after I published my Oh, Jensen piece, it was rapidly obsolete because he resigned and two other affairs came to light. Who knows what else will happen by the time you are reading this ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ I could tell you a lot of things. My mind is like Schrödinger’s cat when it comes to this. I’m both extremely disappointed in Jensen for his behavior and failings, and disappointed that he resigned and the trajectory of world history will be different because of it (right, I mean, if you think about how much leverage this powerful tech has on *everything*). I’m sure you’ve followed the coverage and commentary. It’s been hard to avoid. So I won’t recap all the facts and arguments. Instead, I’ll tell you my read on the situation, and I think Ben Thompson (💚 🥃 🎩) nailed it when he wrote : Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, 2026. He had been CEO of the company ever since he founded it on April 5, 1993. Nvidia started out as a graphics card company; Huang’s exit — nominally because of affairs with a buyer who may or may not have been a Chinese spy, as well as at least two company employees — was ultimately because Nvidia was, by the powers that be, considered a defense contractor, and Huang never adjusted. It’s hard to remember how fast everything happened, because it simultaneously feels fast and long. How long ago was the ancient GPT-4o? Remember how much of a splash that made? That’s 2.5 years ago. Or o1? Remember the big 🍓 brouhaha? That was about two years ago. Decades happened in the past three years, it seems like. Some things can go fast, but some things take time. Not long ago, Nvidia was basically a video game company that cared immensely about the latest Call of Duty or Cyberpunk 2077 releases (🎮). They went from floating on a side island in the tech world (they were rarely mentioned along with the rest of Big Tech) to central to EVERYTHING in basically no time. Google and Microsoft and Amazon had many years to figure out how to be big. How to deal with politicians and their role in geopolitics. And even with all that extra time, they each had their own struggles and moments of crisis. Jensen was thrown into it, and it’s not like he wasn’t also busy with the tech side of things. But on the side, he became a global rockstar and power broker, reshaping industries with his decisions and shifting the balance of power between countries with his chips. That’s got to make your head spin. 😵‍💫 Not to excuse, but maybe to explain . Maybe Jensen spent his whole career driving like a Formula 1 racer. He was incredibly good at it. But somewhere along the way, the closed circuit racetrack became a public highway, and he was still driving the same way. 🏎️ Jensen had extraordinary foresight about tech. What about everything else? Maybe the qualities that made him so incredibly effective as a founder and tech CEO were the same that contributed to his downfall ( your strengths are your weaknesses ). The whole ‘ 60-direct reports 1 , F1 car finely tuned to be driven by Jensen ’ thing made them operate at startup speed and leverage Jensen’s own talent in a way that it may have been diluted in a company with more process and bureaucracy. But it also meant that so much was going through him. It was built to take maximum advantage of his strengths, which means it became highly dependent on his judgement as the flip side of that coin. What happens when that judgement fails? 😬 Just yesterday, Nvidia announced a board-level committee to oversee national-security and export-control compliance. Was he prioritizing Nvidia’s commercial success (as a founder who has the scars of multiple near-bankruptcies would) even as some powerful national-security officials increasingly expected the company to play ball and be a centerpiece of their national-security strategy against China? You can agree or disagree with his arguments for selling older/hobbled chips to China, but it’s possible that those who disagreed with him used what they knew about him to get him out of their way. We don’t know who leaked what, or why, but there’s clearly been a power struggle in Washington, and Jensen being gone was a big win for those pushing for tighter restrictions. What will happen next? ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ The camps are clear. Many shareholders and players in the tech industry are pushing for him to come back, while others in positions of power (including Treasury Secretary Bessent) clearly want him to stay away. Jensen has said he’s open to return , but it’s just one of the many preconditions required. On the earnings call yesterday, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said that the board doesn’t intend to bring him back . We don’t know if more revelations will come out and reshuffle the deck or if the board will be convinced there’s a path somehow… This isn’t over. I’ll leave you on Tobi Lütke on Jensen (and donating blood to three hospitals to be able to buy a Riva TNT GPU 🩸): 📊 Two Questions Going into Anthropic’s IPO 🤔 There are a lot of questions to ask about Anthropic as a business going into its IPO, but two keep coming back to me. I don’t know the answers, but sometimes the questions are what matters most, and over time, as we watch things closely, maybe we’ll find answers. 1. Is Anthropic becoming a platform businesses build around or a supplier they can swap out? 🕸️ I’m sure you’ve seen the line from Anthropic’s S-1 about how over 80% of its Q3 revenue came from models released in the preceding six months. There are a couple of ways to interpret that. 🔀 One is that these things have a very short half-life and there’s very little loyalty to a model and users will just go to what’s best for them. But another possibility is that Anthropic is replacing its own models without losing its customers . Even if any particular model’s advantage only lasts a few months, customers may keep moving to the next Claude because they trust Anthropic to stay competitive. Model-version turnover is not customer churn. 🔄 What I’m curious about is what happens when another lab has a clear lead for a while. Do Anthropic’s customers jump ship, or do they stick around waiting for the next Claude because they trust Anthropic to catch up quickly, so it’s not worth switching? 2. How much of Anthropic’s research spending buys growth and how much is to keep it competitive? 💰 🤷‍♂️ 💸 Serving inference may be super profitable, but what does it cost to keep making the models that customers want to buy? The numbers give us some idea of the scale. According to Anthropic's S-1 (which got an update yesterday to reveal the size of Google and Amazon’s stakes: 13.7% and 14.7% respectively), in the first nine months of 2026, it generated $33.2 billion in revenue with $4.8 billion in cost of revenue (mostly compute to serve customers). But it also had $19.2 billion in R&D expenses , including compute for developing models, research, internal usage, and personnel. Are they spending so much to press their advantage because they believe this will become a winner-take-all or duopoly market? Or are they spending that much because they have to, just to avoid falling behind OpenAI, Meta, Google, etc.? Of course, I suspect it’s not binary and there’s some of both, but the proportions can make a BIG difference to the economics of the business. If even the cheaper, non-frontier models can do most things, why would anyone keep paying a premium for the very best? Maybe because mistakes can be expensive. 💣⚠️💥 If using a cheaper model means spending hours checking and fixing its work, or risking lost revenue because something went wrong, paying more for some overkill model could actually be the cheaper option overall. So maybe the frontier will remain worth paying for even when the models a generation or two behind it are incredibly capable. From the full feed 🔒: The AI Boom Meets Its Political Bottleneck 🧪🔬 Liberty Labs 🧬 🔭 🏴‍☠️🔐 Alex Stamos: AI is Breaking Cybersecurity, So Why Not Rebuild Linux? Alex Stamos is someone worth listening to when it comes to cybersecurity. He spent decades in the field. He was the top security executive at Yahoo and Facebook (you may have heard his name because he helped investigate Russian interference in the 2016 U.S. election), he founded the Stanford Internet Observatory, and teaches cybersecurity at Stanford. He's now chief security officer at Cognition, the AI coding company. He’s on the frontlines. He recently spoke with Nilay Patel on Decoder and I really enjoyed the interview. Here are some highlights: - 💰 The Economics of Cybersecurity Are Breaking Alex Stamos: We’re going to have to lower the cost of defense . You’re completely right to look at this economic problem because what’s happening is attacks are becoming agentic. The cost per token for attackers is going towards zero, and the cost of defense for defenders is staying quite high . It is very important for us to find ways for defenders to have cheaper options. I think that is critical. That’s something I am personally extremely focused on. To be frank, very few people are. […] But for those models, we need to do a lot more work to optimize them and we need to make them cheap. I have a colleague who works at one of the large security platform companies who said that doing an investigation on one of the big frontier model cyber models costs $900 on their product to do an investigation. That is not going to work when the Russian ransomware guys are either using Macs or they’re using throwaway crypto mining rigs and their marginal cost is zero. At the end of the day, Economics 101 rules everything. There’s an asymmetry between attackers and defenders . Attackers don’t need a high success rate, they just need to find one weakness they can exploit. Defenders have to protect against many different kinds of attacks, detect the ones that get through, and contain the damage. -🐧🤖 Google and Amazon Should Rewrite Linux in Rust That was my favorite part of the interview and I’d love to see that actually happen. Alex Stamos: If you’re looking at your code base and you scan it and you’ve got 10,000 bugs, then probably now we are at the point where rewriting it is actually cheaper. […] I wish […] Google would take all of those incredibly brilliant engineers and just tell them, “Take the Linux kernel and rewrite this in Rust.” That would be their gift to the world. […] And then just release it and call it whatever you want, the G Linux kernel, just like they did this with OpenSSL. And I would run that. Cognition would run that on our servers or have Google and Amazon do it together and it would cost them $100 million , but compared to the societal cost that this is costing us every time we have to patch the Linux kernel and you have to reboot every Linux machine on the entire planet, that’s what has to happen. Nilay Patel: I don’t think anyone’s in that position. I don’t think Linus Torvalds is in that position. Alex Stamos: No, I think Sundar Pichai and Andy Jassy are. But the good thing is that a huge number of the really important uses of Linux kernel are production server hardware. So fork it. Linus will never do it because Linus wants to support all that stuff and he’s got all these politics, but Google and Amazon don’t have to care about Linus Torvalds. I like these big ambitious ideas. I mean, coding models are now so good, and if they’re not good enough now, what about in six months or a year? We should seriously consider rewriting some of the central pieces of infrastructure that everything else depends on, using safer languages like Rust. It’s a little like the classic XKCD: We now have the tools to make a much more stable base to that block tower. Stamos isn’t proposing that Google and Amazon support every obscure piece of hardware ever made, either. His idea is to focus on the production server hardware they actually use, while keeping compatibility with the software running above the kernel. Even if it costs a billion dollars, or several billion, it could be a fantastic investment if it significantly reduces the security problems and maintenance burden of one of the most important pieces of infrastructure in the world. 💾 🛡️🤖 🌐 OpenAI + NATO OpenAI announced that NATO is already using its advanced cybersecurity models through Daybreak to find vulnerabilities, investigate suspicious activity, and help develop and test fixes. Usage has reached up to 300 billion tokens per month (inputs + outputs — which sounds like a lot, but now that I think of it, my own Codex use is a few tens of billions of tokens, so I guess it’s not that much 🤔). Maybe they’re counting differently or that number isn’t right. Anyway, that’s being put to work defending critical infrastructure. OpenAI also says that ENISA, the EU’s cybersecurity agency, used its models to identify four vulnerabilities in software used across EU institutions, and all four have been patched . WSJ : As geopolitical tensions remain elevated, the alliance is grappling with increasingly sophisticated threats, particularly in cyberspace: a cyberattack recently targeted European supermarket refrigerators and freezers, causing tens of millions of dollars in damage from spoiled food and equipment failures. Hey, I wrote about that ! This is also being deployed in Ukraine to harden against Russian cyberattacks: The company said in September that Ukraine’s Ministry of Digital Transformation would use Daybreak to protect civilian infrastructure, providing access to tools to identify software vulnerabilities and develop and test fixes more quickly. 👎👎 Are GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra Duds? 🤔 The model roulette can be a frustrating game. You may love a model version, but that doesn’t mean the next one will be anything like it. It’s a good reminder of how much of these LLMs are still black box, more ‘grown’ than designed. Sometimes you get the recipe just right and it tastes wonderful (like Opus 4.6, which was loved for its creativity, conversational intelligence, and personality, or Opus 5.5, which is a reliable workhorse). But sometimes, for whatever reason, it doesn’t come together, and you get models that people don’t like (even if the benchmark numbers are impressive… or on the other side of the ledge, Opus 5 and 4.7. OpenAI has its own equivalents of this, with GPT-5.6 Sol on one side and GPT-5 on the other). This is pure speculation, but with Anthropic’s IPO coming, and the recent release of Fable 5.2, OpenAI probably had a lot of pressure to come out with something. Maybe it wasn’t quite fully baked yet, but they released GPT 6.2 Sol and Astra, and so far the reaction from most of those with early access has been…. Not great, Bob So normally I would tell you more about how the model has improved on certain benchmarks and how its architecture is different or whatever. But today the most notable news is really the vibes. Matt ended changing his mind and posting this VERY negative review: I haven’t had enough time with them to have a real opinion yet, so stay tuned for my review. Tibo at OpenAI said that many of these reviews were done some days ago, and that they’ve since improved the model (probably by tweaking the system prompts). I don’t know how much they can do with just that. They may have to rush out 6.3 if they can make it better on those aspects… But at this time, 6.2 certainly appears to be a gift for Anthropic’s IPO. From the full feed 🔒: Microsoft and AI-Assisted ASIC Design 🎨 🎭 Liberty Studio 👩‍🎨 🎥 ⚔️🛡️ Watching the Lord of the Rings Trilogy with my Kids 🏰 I thought I would have to wait longer to watch these films with my kids, but I’ve learned a lot about what they can handle and can’t handle in recent times as we’ve watched all kinds of other films, and I decided they were ready. We watched the extended editions, which add up to 11h23mins (!!). It was more like watching a TV series than films, watching an hour at a time over a few weeks. They loved it. They had never seen anything quite that epic, and at various points I could see them get so carried away and excited that they would almost vibrate on the couch next to me. It was beautiful to see. For my part, I’m not the kind of nerd who re-watches these films often. I had seen all of them in theater when they came out. When I saw Fellowship, I had not read the books, so it kind of blew my mind. Then, I read the trilogy before seeing Two Towers and I remember being slightly disappointed by it. I enjoyed it, but when the books are fresh in your memory, it’s harder to appreciate the films for what they are. And somehow I had forgotten large parts of Return of the King . I didn’t remember the falling skulls and the Green Ghost Army and all that stuff. The films held up pretty well. Some of the effects have aged a little bit. I remember when I first saw Gollum, I thought he looked incredible. So photorealistic! And now when I look at him, he looks more like a video game character at times. Good thing that the performance by Andy Serkis is so good that it makes you forget about that, even today. We’ve come a long way with how we integrate 3D characters into scenes with subtle light effects and ray tracing and all that. It almost makes me wish there could be a remastered version where everything would be kept the same but some of the effects would be improved. I know this doesn’t always have a great track record (*cough* George Lucas), but maybe it could work here. 🤔 1 Btw, this phrase about 60 direct reports has been said so often that I rarely even take the time to think about it. But sixty people, each with a whole multi-thousand group of people around them working on very complex things (chips, supply chain, partnerships, software, R&D, financial deals, global compliance, etc). That’s a lot of people and that’s a lot of complex things to deal with on a daily basis.
