items.body: https://t.co/CYB0vLZOxi TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/18/26 The board story split in this window. Semafor reported that a minority faction of Nvidia directors is still pushing to bring Jensen Huang back, one day after the chair stated on the record that the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him. Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott confirmed on air that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have both agreed to appear before his committee, with no date set. The Information placed Nvidia's longtime sales chief, Jay Puri, in direct customer relations with Alice Huang, identified the Cenly Chen in the Muddy Waters photograph question as Puri's wife and a former longtime Super Micro senior executive, and reported that Nvidia's own sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice in 2022. Reuters documented a proxy access route by which Huang can nominate two directors. A filings based analysis put hard dates on the delayed Form 10-Q. A BOARD FACTION FOR A RETURN • Semafor reported late on November 17, 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that a minority faction of Nvidia directors is still pushing to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, even after Chair Harvey Jones stated on the November 17 earnings call that the board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him. This is Semafor's reporting, carried here as reported: the Semafor article itself was not read firsthand, and the claim rests on several independent summaries of it that agree on every material specific. • Per that reporting, Huang met with numerous tech executives and spoke with at least one Nvidia director about returning before the earnings report and before his November 17 public statement, and co-author Reed Albergotti described one three-person faction as vehemently against a return. Both positions are reported inside the same board: a minority pushing for a return, and a faction vehemently against one, against the chair's on the record statement that the acceptance was unanimous and reinstatement is not intended. The reported push is not a board act, and the chair's statement stands as made. • In the same Semafor report, other directors are narrowing the permanent CEO search: Arm CEO Rene Haas has spoken with some directors about the role but is concerned about the optics of taking the job amid calls to bring Huang back, and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy has also been considered, though it is unclear whether Murphy could take the job while Marvell works through its merger with Lumentum. No offer has been confirmed, and Nvidia, Huang, Arm and Marvell did not comment. Haas was already in the record as a reported board consideration; the direct talks and the optics concern are new, and Murphy and Marvell are new names in the matter. THE SENATE DATES ARE AGREED • Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott said on CNBC's Squawk Box on November 18, 2026 that Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee and that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify: "They both have agreed. We will hopefully have this done before Christmas." The quotation is carried identically by CNBC and the New York Post, both read in full. • The appearance Scott asked for is a public hearing, not a closed door interview, and no hearing date has been set. December 3 for Huang and December 10 for Lutnick were the requested dates in Scott's letters, which carried a subpoena warning for Huang. The Senate appearances are therefore agreed, with the date unset, where the prior record carried them only as requests with the subpoena warning standing, and a relay attribution of an agreement in the prior window was expressly not carried as corroborated. • Scott also said on air: "They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the entity list. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security didn't do it, Howard didn't do it, we want to know why." A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment on Scott's announcement. PURI, ALICE HUANG AND CENLY CHEN • The Information reported on November 18, 2026, in a story by Qianer Liu and Phoebe Liu, that Ajay "Jay" Puri, Nvidia's longtime sales chief and EVP Worldwide Field Operations until June 2026, handled customer relations with Alice Huang. The article body is paywalled and was not read firsthand; the finding is stated directly by the outlet's own reporter in her own post. Puri was previously in this record only through the Muddy Waters photograph question; this is the first reporting placing Nvidia's sales chief in direct customer relations with Alice Huang. • In the same story, the reporter states: "Puri is married to Cenly Chen, a former longtime senior executive at Supermicro. In March, U.S. prosecutors charged two Supermicro executives with conspiring to smuggle banned Nvidia servers to China. Chen was not charged with wrongdoing. She left the company in April." This answers, at reported grade from a named outlet and not from a primary source, the identity question Muddy Waters expressly left unverified: whether the Cenly Chen photographed with Puri in public between 2024 and 2026 is the former Super Micro executive of that name. The Information identifies her as Puri's wife and as that former longtime senior executive. Chen was not charged with wrongdoing. THE ALIBABA INTRODUCTIONS • The Information also reported that Nvidia's sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang on two occasions in 2022, months before United States export controls on advanced chips took effect, according to three people with direct knowledge of the matter. Two of them said the introductions helped Huang and her company win Alibaba as a customer, and that deal helped launch her business: with Alibaba on board she was able to get bank loans to finance buying more Nvidia chips. This is reported grade, on a single source chain: the article body is paywalled and unread, and the reporting was read through a full summary carriage. • The record already held Alibaba as an end user of the Litong network, a financing layer, and Megaspeed's representation to Nvidia that Alibaba would be an anchor customer. It did not hold Nvidia's own sales team making the introductions that landed Alibaba, or the introductions' role in financing her chip purchases. HUANG'S PROXY ACCESS ROUTE • Reuters reported on November 17, 2026, in an article read in full, that Jensen Huang has the ability to nominate two directors to the Nvidia board ahead of the company's annual shareholder meeting and vote, according to company proxy and corporate filings: any shareholder or group owning more than 3 percent of the voting power for at least three years may nominate directors for inclusion in the company's proxy materials, Huang and entities tied to him have owned more than 3 percent for more than three years, and he currently owns roughly 3.5 percent of the company. • Nominees must qualify as independent directors, would go on Nvidia's proxy ballot, and are not guaranteed seats, because shareholders vote. Nvidia may leave out a nominee who has violated the company's bylaws and charter, and Reuters could not determine whether Huang's conduct broke the bylaws or charter. Nvidia and a representative for Huang did not respond to requests for comment. No prior claim in the record records this nomination right, which is the mechanical route by which Huang could place allies on the board at the annual meeting, typically in June, regardless of the current board's position. This filing is a catch-up: an earlier Reuters post of the same article fell inside the prior window and was not filed there. THE 10-Q CLOCK • A filings based analysis by an independent analyst account, citing SEC records, documents Nvidia's Form 10-Q timing: Nvidia filed its full quarterly report within 44 minutes of results nine straight times, the streak running from August 2024 to August 2026 with a median gap of 14 minutes 41 seconds and a longest gap of 43 minutes 52 seconds. Before that streak it often filed 2 to 7 days after results. This is reported grade: a single analyst account citing SEC records, and the streak was not independently recomputed from EDGAR. • On those figures, a filing after November 24, 2026 would be Nvidia's longest wait between results and a quarterly report in the commission's records since at least 2020, the longest so far being 7 days, in August 2022. The legal deadline is December 4, 2026, 40 days after the October 25 quarter end, and a late notice can stretch it to December 9 only if Nvidia files that notice and says the delay could not be avoided without unreasonable effort or expense. Nvidia has missed no deadline and has not linked the timing to any investigation or to its auditor. The cause of the timing is undocumented, and speculation attributing it to the investigation is not carried here. THE CHECKPOINTS • November 18, 2026: the closed door briefing, today, with no outcome reporting in this window. • November 24, 2026: Bennet's answers due, and the 10-Q streak break marker, after which a filing would be the longest wait since at least 2020 on the reported figures. • About November 25, 2026: Bessent's 10 day deadline for answers from Nvidia's board and outside counsel. • December 1, 2026: Huang's closed door transcribed interview with the three House committees, reported as agreed, and the House Foreign Affairs Democrats' answers due. • December 2, 2026: Teter's closed door transcribed interview, reported as agreed. • December 3, 2026: the Foreign Affairs hearing with Under Secretary Kessler. • December 4, 2026: the Form 10-Q legal deadline, extendable to December 9 only with a late notice. • Date not set: the Senate Banking public hearing with Huang and Lutnick, both agreed to appear, which Scott said he hopes to complete before Christmas. • January 8, 2027: lead plaintiff deadline in Kistenmacher v. NVIDIA. • January 10, 2027: the current suspension of the September 2025 subsidiary rule ends, per the Cantwell letter.

external_articles.title: Jensengate | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
The fall of Jensen Huang at Nvidia, tracked in twelve-hour editions: the newest edition in full at the top, and every earlier edition in the archive below.

TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10AM TO 10PM on 11/18/26

Congress widened on every front in this window. A fourth House committee, Energy and Commerce, sent oversight letters to Nvidia and to Commerce leadership with a December 2 briefing deadline. At the Aspen Cyber Summit, a Select Committee member publicly called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to go, and three House Democrats opened an inquiry into whether the Secretary's family firm interests influenced the decision to keep Megaspeed off the Entity List. Inside Nvidia, the Wall Street Journal's account of an employee letter to the full board arguing that irreplaceable talent is contemplating departing was filed as a catch-up, employees met in the first all-hands since the resignation, and Nvidia's quarterly lobbying disclosure set a record. The November 18 closed door briefing produced no public readout in this window.

The board story split in this window. Semafor reported that a minority faction of Nvidia directors is still pushing to bring Jensen Huang back, one day after the chair stated on the record that the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him. Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott confirmed on air that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have both agreed to appear before his committee, with no date set. The Information placed Nvidia's longtime sales chief, Jay Puri, in direct customer relations with Alice Huang, identified the Cenly Chen in the Muddy Waters photograph question as Puri's wife and a former longtime Super Micro senior executive, and reported that Nvidia's own sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice in 2022. Reuters documented a proxy access route by which Huang can nominate two directors. A filings based analysis put hard dates on the delayed Form 10-Q.

Huang spoke for himself for the first time since resigning, owning the personal mistakes and saying he would return if the board decided it was best. Hours later the board chair answered on the earnings call: the board unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, and a search firm is retained. The Wall Street Journal reported a new SEC investigation into whether Nvidia disclosures misled investors. The board created a national security and export control oversight committee. Earnings beat and guidance rose, with no 10-Q filed with the release. The December House interview dates are now reported as agreed, and Muddy Waters disclosed a short with an expressly unverified identity question at its center.

The window brought the first official government account of the Megaspeed investigation. The Commerce and Justice Departments issued a joint statement setting out their timeline and putting the Justice Department in the lead on the criminal investigation, while making no allegation against Nvidia or Jensen Huang and saying nothing on the Entity List question. On the return question, reporting now has the board not considering bringing Huang back, the opposite direction from the comeback reporting in the record. President Trump and Vice President Vance both cast doubt on the claim that Alice Huang was a spy. In the Senate, the Commerce Committee's ranking member put four alleged export control failures in writing to Secretary Lutnick, and a Republican senator introduced a bill to force a listing decision on Megaspeed within 30 days. The shareholder case against Nvidia and Huang widened by amended complaint.

In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule closing the remote access channel at the center of the Megaspeed business model, and imposed a new destination license requirement covering Singapore and Malaysia, Megaspeed's two operating jurisdictions. The Straits Times reported the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case, a police search of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary that found empty server racks and no chips. President Trump publicly welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, in the opposite direction from his Treasury secretary's push for an outside chief executive.

In this window the succession fight split in public on the same Sunday shows that moved the congressional track. Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the three House committees, with no subpoena needed and the date still being discussed. A briefed Gang of Eight member said on the record that the intelligence community does not know whether Alice Huang was a witting asset. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent directed the board toward an outside chief executive and set it a 10-day deadline to answer on export-compliance culture, while the Financial Times reported Huang himself is discussing a comeback, with an ally war room lobbying for his return.

In this window the channel record widened again: the Wall Street Journal reported records showing Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion of top Nvidia chips to companies in China, a fifth chip figure with its own window, and reported an unwritten Nvidia rule capping partners' Chinese customers and a new channel node, Aolani Cloud. Megaspeed answered publicly for the first time on Alice Huang, saying she left the company effective August 30, 2025 and that it has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The Washington Post reported Huang is quietly helping pick his own successor, and Elon Musk said many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Huang personally.

In this window the fight over the classified memo at the center of the case widened: the Washington Post reported the memo was Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recasting of a CIA report in more assertive terms, and CNN reported the CIA is not yet convinced the intercepts prove Alice Huang knowingly funneled information to Beijing. The Financial Times reported Nvidia carries directors and officers insurance that protects its directors personally and not the company, filings show a director sold about $946.6 million of stock in the weeks before the board inquiry opened, and Reuters reported Chinese AI firms are racing to reserve Nvidia powered capacity outside China before the remote rental loophole closes. South Korea said Nvidia has reconfirmed its 260,000 GPU supply plan after the resignation, Bill Ackman defended Huang on presumption of innocence grounds, and the first Sunday show booking for a case chair was announced for tomorrow.

Overnight, Reuters reported that Jensen Huang told Nvidia's own general counsel and chief marketing officer in writing that his interactions with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business dealings, the House chairs' 8 p.m. deadline for his written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public, and a filings-based reconstruction put $5,353 million of Nvidia's formerly Singapore-billed revenue with China and Hong Kong headquartered buyers. Super Micro denied on the record that Megaspeed was ever its customer, a sitting administration official argued Huang should have been warned the way a congressman once was, and the street kept repricing the overhang: HSBC cut its target by more than half, and a billionaire holder said he will make no further investment in Nvidia without Huang.

Today the fight over the Megaspeed Entity List delay became an open cabinet split, the Commerce Secretary's own tenure came into question, Reuters documented the scale of Chinese AI projects built around restricted Nvidia chips, and the succession search moved in public for the first time: the board was reported to have approached an external candidate, then issued its first statement calling candidate speculation premature, while two major holders asked the board to slow the process down and keep Jensen Huang's return on the table. The 8 p.m. deadline for Huang's written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public.

THE SUCCESSION SEARCH MOVES, THEN THE BOARD PUSHES BACK

Overnight, the House turned its request to Jensen Huang into an ultimatum with a deadline tonight, the Senate Banking subpoena threat was verified from the letter itself and shown to run to Huang only, Bloomberg published the first account of how the admission and the resignation decision actually happened, Malaysia opened its own official inquiry into the Megaspeed channel while its prime minister said there is no indication so far that chips were exported from Malaysia, and CNN's reporting reframed the Alice Huang spy question toward recruitment after access.

The first full day after Jensen Huang's resignation widened the case on every front at once. Huang agreed to testify before Congress, the Senate Banking Committee requested dated public hearings for Huang and for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the tax committees opened their own investigation with a records preservation demand, the Justice Department spoke on the record for the first time, Singapore published its full account of the Alice Huang investigation, and the channel record added two new end points, DeepSeek and Huawei.

THE TAX COMMITTEES OPEN AN INVESTIGATION

The case resolved overnight. Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately, ending the board process that had built through the night: Semafor had reported some directors favored CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and Kress is the interim appointment in the release. The night also deepened the record behind the case, with the Wall Street Journal's account of the husband who introduced Huang to Alice Huang, Congress turning its fire on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Megaspeed's first public statement, and the analyst downgrade wave broadening before the announcement landed.

In twelve hours the case moved from congressional pressure to the boardroom. The New York Times reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with a direct report. The Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, and Bloomberg reported a succession search is under way. The committees' 5 PM deadline for his answer on the November 18 briefing passed with no acceptance or alternative date reported, and the desk raised its exit estimate in this window.

Atlas Peak Research. Compiled from public reporting, company statements, and congressional and court records. Each edition covers twelve hours of the case and appears here in full.

Updated 11/18/26 10:08 PM ET · 14 editions

items.title: $NVDA NVIDIA: WHAT THE BROKER CALLBACKS ADDED AFTER THE PRINT The print and the earnings call carried the numbers. The management callbacks that followed carried the fine print. Th
items.body: $NVDA NVIDIA: WHAT THE BROKER CALLBACKS ADDED AFTER THE PRINT The print and the earnings call carried the numbers. The management callbacks that followed carried the fine print. This is only what the callbacks added, bank by bank, with everything that was already in the release or on the call stripped out. THE 10-Q DELAY UBS (Buy, $220 target, cut from $240) is the only bank that reports asking directly: "When queried on our callback, management indicated this was related to the ongoing investigation and whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing." The company has said only that the 10-Q will be filed "in the coming weeks," later than usual. Citi's callback account matches: the delay was attributed to certain matters related to an ongoing investigation, and management reiterated confidence in the financials. Read together: the open item is risk-factor drafting. The 10-Q, when it lands, is a document to read for new risk language, not for revised numbers. UBS's own worry runs the other way: the bank flags a real risk that Nvidia "becomes beholden to these purchase commitments and has to keep throwing money at its customers to drive revenue," and notes calendar 2028 supply commitments did not increase significantly. CHINA AND HOPPER Citi's callback detail: by customer headquarters, China was about 10% of revenue in the quarter ended October, and that figure includes gaming, workstations and automotive, so data center China was a subset. Management does not plan to ship any more H20 or H200 products. The resulting sequential revenue headwind is more than $2 billion and is already reflected in the $130 billion January-quarter guide. The impact of the restrictions on shipments to certain countries and on remote access is currently not material and is also in the guide. KeyBanc (Sector Weight) carries the same line in shorter form: Nvidia is no longer shipping H200 to China. Goldman's note: Nvidia is no longer shipping permissible Hopper products to China, full stop. Cantor Fitzgerald adds the forward piece: the updated calendar 2027 guide includes zero China contribution and already reflects the company's initial work on the new BIS rules on sales to Southeast Asian cloud providers. Barclays notes the gap: the company did not explicitly comment on China's indirect access through Southeast Asia, and that remains an overhang into calendar 2027. Three callbacks, one conclusion: Hopper to China is finished, not paused. THE GUARANTEE BOOK, IN FULL Yorkville Ives (Outperform, $225) has the most granular account of the callback language on commitments: Nvidia will continue to be disciplined and selective and is rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees; land, power and shell is the top priority for any future support; prepayment arrangements would be considered for investment-grade customers; guarantees start only once a neocloud has secured its financing and the capacity is deployed and accepted; and capital goes to suppliers and the buyback first. KeyBanc's version of the same clarification: the $32B of neocloud obligations backstops only customers who have secured financing, and otherwise the commitments could be reduced or eliminated. Wells Fargo (Overweight, $250 target, cut from $300) supplies the balance-sheet frame: purchase commitments expanded to $390B exiting the quarter, up $111B sequentially; inventory plus purchase commitments total $429.7B, up $119B; neocloud commitments $32B, down $4B sequentially; power and systems credit support guarantees $9.5B; neocloud land, power and shell guarantees $3.5B. Citi: the company will be more selective about guaranteeing compute rentals for emerging cloud providers. Goldman: guarantees and commitments will continue, in a disciplined and selective manner. The pattern across five banks is consistent because it is the same callback script: conditionality first, totals second. The backstop is conditional and shrinking at the margin, which is a different picture from the headline guarantee totals. RENTAL RATES AND THE $2.5 TRILLION Jefferies (Buy, $250 target, cut from $300): cloud industry backlog reached $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months ago. Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price. B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. Jefferies reads the rental rates as tangible evidence that available supply remains well below demand. Their caution is durability: the growth trajectory is linked to spending by the leading AI labs and continued evidence of AI return on investment, factors largely outside Nvidia's control. Citi's clarification stands against the backlog figure: it is an aggregate reported by the cloud providers, not Nvidia's own backlog. None of the rental figures were on the main call. SEGMENT DETAIL DA Davidson (Buy, $200): the hyperscaler segment grew 23.5% sequentially to $60B, 13.5% above consensus, and management attributed the outperformance to the Vera Rubin ramp. AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise came in at $47.5B, up about 18% sequentially and about 127.5% year over year, missing estimates by roughly 3%. The release and the call carried the data center total; this split comes from the notes. ANALYST MATH AND FRAMING Melius (Hold, $185): the extra week in the January quarter accounts for about $9 to $10B of the roughly $14B sequential increase in guidance, against about $20B of sequential growth in the October quarter; guidance still came in about $5B above consensus. Melius calls the fiscal 2028 raise the real surprise: 500 basis points, about $45B of revenue on the higher base, delivered in exactly the year when the new BIS restrictions and neocloud capital shortages should bite, which they read as hyperscalers taking whatever they can get. Aletheia Capital (Hold): off-balance-sheet commitments surged nearly $60B sequentially to $224B by their accounting, a different measure from the company's guarantee figures, and they stay on the sidelines pending clarity on the earnings outlook and the incoming CEO's strategic direction. Barclays (Overweight, $210): reported-quarter gross margin came in nearly 100 basis points above the Street on a richer Blackwell Ultra mix despite the initial Rubin ramp, and consistent demand messaging left them more positive, with leadership still in limbo. Stifel (Buy, $205) draws three second-order takes: Nvidia's capital is pivoting from customer financing toward supplier prepayments, positive for substrate, packaging, EMS and optical capacity; networking above $21B with CPO in volume production broadens optical content (that characterization is Stifel's, not a company quote); and with fiscal 2028 growth capped by supply rather than demand, unmet demand opens the door to second sources. Morgan Stanley (Overweight, $260 target, cut from $267) had expected a real chance of no fiscal 2028 update at all given the Commerce, DOJ, SEC and internal investigations, and even after the raise to 75% growth they hold their own 2027 growth estimate at 56%, raised from 52%, explicitly more cautious than management. THE SKEPTIC CAMP Summit Insights downgraded to Hold from Buy: the leadership change creates uncertainty around the roadmap beyond Vera Rubin, the Commerce ruling can cause unintended negative consequences across the AI ecosystem in 2027, and custom ASICs gain share in 2027 as supply capacity frees up. HSBC (Hold, $170): the beat was not the focus; investors wanted confidence instilled, and there is limited room for a re-rating until a permanent succession plan is laid out and new leadership demonstrates execution capability. Truist (Hold, $174): more questions than answers, and the three hardest questions were not asked on the call: how much revenue the new Commerce rules might curtail, the effect of the US political power shift on land, power and shell availability over the next one to two years, and the status of the CEO direct-report engagement. Piper Sandler (Overweight, $230 target, cut from $300) raised fiscal 2027 and 2028 EPS by 5% and 9% but cut its target multiple to about 10x calendar 2028 earnings from 14x on CEO transition uncertainty, calling the roughly 10x calendar 2027 multiple a long-term buying opportunity while expecting the stock to stay range-bound until succession clears. WHAT THE CALLBACKS DID NOT PRODUCE No callback surfaced anything on succession timing or the CEO search process, and no bank quantified the Commerce remote-access rules beyond Cantor's note that the updated guide already reflects the company's initial work on the Southeast Asia cloud restrictions.

items.title: $AAOI announces another $550M ATM. Investors are furious. The stock crashes 14.3% to $38.77 and is now down more than 83% from its 52-week high. What next? I've seen plenty of inve
items.body: $AAOI announces another $550M ATM. Investors are furious. The stock crashes 14.3% to $38.77 and is now down more than 83% from its 52-week high. What next? I've seen plenty of investors saying they've had enough of this company and are selling their shares. I understand their frustration. I really do. But is this actually the best moment to sell? I'm not selling. I invested in $AAOI after several rounds of dilution because I saw an enormous manufacturing ramp ahead in an industry where demand is significantly outpacing supply. And that hasn't changed. So why should I suddenly react emotionally just because the stock price has collapsed? Especially when AAOI ended Q3 with $621.5M in cash, investments and restricted cash, and revenue growing 127.5% YoY. That doesn't mean the company is financially comfortable. Its expansion requires enormous amounts of capital. But the opportunity I invested in is still there. Let's talk about management. I'll agree with anyone who says management has made some terrible decisions. Announcing another ATM at these prices, right after the Jensen controversy and around NVIDIA earnings, is another example of awful timing. And that's not even my biggest concern. Take the recently signed LTA with a major hyperscaler. A three-year agreement covering at least 10% of that customer's 1.6T transceiver requirements, with an estimated value of $1–1.5B. Sounds great. But where are the customer prepayments? Why are shareholders financing the manufacturing expansion while hyperscalers secure future supply? I'd much rather see customers participating in financing the capacity they're going to need. Management is also negotiating another LTA that could potentially be more than five times larger. I'm hoping that agreement, if signed, has a very different financing structure. Then there's the decision to purchase buildings AAOI had previously leased. Owning your manufacturing facilities is generally a good thing. It secures the locations, creates collateral for financing, and potentially gives you more flexibility to modernize and expand production. But when you're already raising enormous amounts of capital, buying real estate you could continue leasing doesn't seem like the smartest use of cash. That's money you could have spread over several years. Maybe the economics of those purchases will eventually justify the decision. I'd like to see the numbers. Now let's look at the valuation. At $38.77 per share and approximately 90.77M shares outstanding, $AAOI has a market cap of around $3.52B. If management fully uses the new $550M ATM at roughly this price, it would add approximately 14.2M shares, bringing the total to around 105M shares. That's another 15.6% increase in the share count. And yes, I'm frustrated about it. But here's what matters to my investment thesis. AAOI expects to reach a monthly data center revenue run rate of approximately $471M toward the end of 2027. That's $5.65B annualized. For comparison, the entire company is currently valued at just $3.52B. Of course, a revenue run rate isn't the same as annual revenue, and revenue isn't profit. But the difference between today's valuation and the scale management is targeting is enormous. Even assuming further dilution, I can see a scenario where $AAOI is worth 4–5 times its current market cap. My bullish target remains $200 per share by the end of 2027. At 120M shares, that would mean a $24B market cap, or roughly 4.25x the targeted annualized data center revenue. Aggressive? Absolutely. And it would require the market to assign AAOI a premium valuation based on its growth, margins and future earnings potential. But I don't consider it impossible. The condition is simple: management has to deliver. Now look at the manufacturing ramp. AAOI expects Q4 2026 revenue of $385–420M. Manufacturing capacity increased from approximately 200K transceivers per month at the end of Q2 to nearly 330K around Q3, with a target of more than 500K by year-end. The original year-end target was 650K. So yes, management has already fallen behind its initial expansion schedule. Construction delays and difficulties securing electrical infrastructure have pushed part of the expansion back by several months. But here's what's interesting. Despite those delays, AAOI raised its end-2027 manufacturing capacity target from 930K to more than 1 million transceivers per month. Its new 210K-square-foot Sugar Land facility is expected to begin initial operations in December. And management suggested modeling data center revenue growth roughly linearly throughout 2027, from around $100M per month in Q4 2026 toward $471M per month by year-end. Under that assumption, we're looking at approximately $3.4B in data center revenue alone during 2027. Add CATV, and total company revenue could be considerably higher. That's my scenario based on management's targets, not official annual guidance. And those manufacturing figures represent installed capacity, not guaranteed production or shipments. Now let's talk about the main reason I own this company: demand. The optical networking industry is experiencing extraordinary demand. Hyperscalers are moving toward 1.6T faster than many suppliers anticipated. In fact, one of AAOI's major customers accelerated its transition from 800G to 1.6T faster than AAOI was prepared for. The company already has approximately $400–450M in 1.6T orders, but expects to recognize only $50–70M of 1.6T revenue in Q4 because of DSP supply constraints. Think about that. Customers want the products. AAOI has the orders. But it can't deliver enough of them yet. That's an execution problem, not evidence of weak demand. Of course, execution problems can become very expensive. Especially when customers need capacity now, not six months from now. But AAOI already supplies major hyperscalers. These aren't customers that qualify new optical suppliers overnight. The testing process is rigorous, qualification can take months, and switching suppliers at scale isn't necessarily straightforward. That doesn't make AAOI irreplaceable. But it does give the company an established position in a market where qualified supply is extremely valuable. Management even believes it may be able to satisfy less than 80% of current customer demand after completing its planned expansion. If that assessment is accurate, demand won't be the biggest problem. Delivering the capacity will be. So what now? Let's be clear. $AAOI is an extremely risky investment. Management has made questionable capital allocation decisions. Shareholders have been diluted repeatedly. Construction is delayed. Supply chains remain constrained. Customer concentration is high. And the stock could fall further. A lower share price doesn't automatically make the business safer. But it does change the potential return relative to the price I'm paying. I don't evaluate an investment based on how angry I am about a falling stock price. I don't sell simply because management made another decision I disagree with. I ask myself whether the original investment thesis has changed. And right now, I still see a company with rapidly growing demand, established hyperscaler relationships, and a manufacturing expansion that could transform its revenue base over the next two years. The question is whether management can actually deliver. If they do, I believe the upside from here could be substantial. If they don't, shareholders will pay the price. That's the risk I'm accepting. If you invested in $AAOI, you should have known what kind of volatility you were signing up for. No crying in the casino. I'll try to prepare a much deeper DD on $AAOI if there's enough interest.

items.title: Digital Advertising Industry Snapshot 3Q’26
items.body:
As I do after every quarter, let me share the snapshot of the overall digital advertising industry.

As a reminder, the actual digital advertising industry is larger than what my snapshot below shows, but this snapshot helps me gauge the broader digital advertising industry’s big picture. TikTok and Walmart advertising are notably missing here. Well, TikTok is a private company and Walmart doesn’t disclose their advertising revenue consistently.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!btvD!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F21618841-686d-4959-8191-f888e1943159_1365x1381.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!btvD!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F21618841-686d-4959-8191-f888e1943159_1365x1381.png)

Sources: Company filings, [Daloopa](https://daloopa.com/?utm_source=MBI&utm_medium=Organic&utm_campaign=SourceLink), MBI estimates

**Some key takeaways from 3Q’26:**

Digital advertising industry **decelerated** from 20.2% in 2Q’26 to 16.1% in 3Q’26. As mentioned in my last quarter’s snapshot, given the tough comp I expected both Q3 and Q4 to experience deceleration.

Meta’s incremental share **jumped to 52.7%**. Outside the ATT-distorted 2022 numbers, this is the first time in this snapshot that Meta captured more than half of the incremental dollar. There is a bit of an asterisk here. Amazon moved Prime Day into June this year, so its ad growth slowed from 26% in 2Q’26 to 11% in 3Q’26, which mechanically flatters everyone else’s incremental share. **If I combine 2Q and 3Q, Meta’s incremental share was ~48%.** That is still comfortably ahead of its ~35% current share, so the share gain story remains fully intact even after adjusting for the Prime Day timing.

Google Search’s incremental share **dropped to 27.6%**, the lowest since 2Q’23 (which was again distorted by ATT). Last quarter I **[wondered](https://mbideepdives.substack.com/p/digital-advertising-industry-snapshot-921?utm_source=publication-search)** whether Search could hold ~30% incremental share or would drift toward the mid-20s. But we need to adjust for the Prime Day impact here as well. On a combined 2Q and 3Q basis, Search’s incremental share was just a tad bit below 30%. Let’s wait a couple more quarters to see if Google Search can stay around this level or keep drifting downwards.

Among the sub-scaled players, AppLovin and Reddit are still punching above their weight, with incremental shares of 3.2% and 1.2% against current shares of 1.2% and 0.5% respectively. AppLovin’s growth actually reaccelerated to 56%. Trade Desk’s revenue declined YoY for the first time in this snapshot, and its incremental share is now essentially zero. Snap (0.2% incremental share vs 0.8% current share) continues to lose relevance.

I should, however, note that some of the definitions of advertising here are not quite apple to apple as some companies report advertising dollar on a gross and some report on a net basis which is why I like to focus more on incremental share data.

I would also like to explain some changes for this quarter’s edition.

Digital advertising industry is defined as Alphabet’s advertising revenue+ Meta’s advertising revenue+ Snap’s ad revenue+ Pinterest revenue+ Microsoft Search and advertising revenue+ Amazon advertising revenue+ Trade Desk revenue+ AppLovin revenue+ Reddit’s ad revenue. Microsoft no longer discloses search advertising on its own, so I now use its “Search and advertising” line, which also includes LinkedIn’s ad and Premium subscription revenue. Microsoft restated this line back to 3Q’24, which is why its share steps up from ~2.7% to ~4% in that quarter. All the growth and incremental share numbers compare each quarter with the prior year on the same basis, so Microsoft gets no credit for the definition change. I also replaced Snap’s 2023 total revenue with estimated ad revenue. For 2022, I still assume Snap’s total revenue as their ad revenue, which is perhaps closer to reality anyway. Reddit’s number has only been included since 1Q’23 since we don’t have their ad revenue numbers in earlier years. Keep these in mind while looking at YoY comparisons in the past. Also note that for visual convenience, I have shaded all the Q3 of the last five years.

_Subscribers get the daily journal and five+ years of Deep Dives, i.e. full-length analyses with financial models on **[70](https://mbideepdives.substack.com/p/deep-dives)+** companies. The daily is just how I think out loud between the Deep Dives!_

**Current Portfolio:**

Please note that these are **NOT** my recommendation to buy/sell these securities, but just disclosure from my end so that you can assess potential biases that I may have because of my own personal portfolio holdings. Always consider my write-up my personal investing journal and never forget my objectives, risk tolerance, and constraints may have no resemblance to yours.

items.title: I think 2028 AI capex is more likely to come in 5–15% below consensus. OpenAI and Anthropic are growing revenue too slowly to cover the rent on everything being built for them. By
items.body: I think 2028 AI capex is more likely to come in 5–15% below consensus. OpenAI and Anthropic are growing revenue too slowly to cover the rent on everything being built for them. By my model, the two labs need about $15B of net new ARR every month through 2028 to pay their compute bills. This year they’ve averaged about $10.5B. I started from the landlord’s side. NVIDIA puts a gigawatt of Rubin capacity at about $60B. Depreciate the IT gear over 5 years and the building over 14, charge a 9% cost of capital, add power and operations, and the owner needs roughly $14B a year in rent per GW to break even. That’s on the low side. CoreWeave says its new 4–5 year contracts price at $20–25M per MW. Consensus has the big five cloud providers plus neoclouds spending about $1.0T, $1.6T and $1.8T in 2026–28. After stripping out non-AI spend and capacity they use themselves, I estimate OpenAI and Anthropic will be paying about 70% of the rent on leased-out AI capacity by 2028. Covering that would take about $441B of combined revenue in 2028. At this year’s pace, I estimate they reach about $347B, 21% short. Monthly net new ARR is the number that matters, and it has been choppy even as the base grew. Anthropic’s annualized revenue rose about ninefold this year, yet it added about $16.7B in April, around $3B a month in August and September, and about $10B in October. Token prices roughly halve every year, so usage has to grow about 4x a year just to keep revenue on track. GPU life is the one variable that closes the gap by itself. CoreWeave said Ampere and Hopper pricing rose 30–50% quarter over quarter in Q3. If older chips keep renting at strong prices and servers last 7 years instead of 5, the revenue needed in 2028 falls to about $342B, just under this year’s pace. That has only been tested while compute is scarce, so I keep 5 years as my base case. Most 2027 spending is already under contract, so I expect the adjustment to land on 2028 expansion. Oracle and the neoclouds look most exposed. Analysts estimate OpenAI accounts for roughly half of Oracle’s backlog, and by my math OpenAI alone needs about $90B of outside money to cover 2028 compute, while Anthropic has about $19B to spare. Neoclouds also borrow at higher rates. Financing drives the size of the cut. My base case assumes OpenAI raises about $27B more. With no new money, the 2028 cut widens to 16–26%. With about $65B, consensus holds. A 5–15% cut would slow 2028 GPU and ASIC spending growth from the roughly 46% the market expects to 24–39%. Chipmakers would need less new equipment for 2028–29 capacity, so tool orders could soften first, as early as 2027. Even after that cut, 2028 capex would still run about 50–70% above 2026. I still see AI demand expanding over the long run. Capex expectations got ahead of revenue. Anthropic’s Q4 roadshow guidance implies the two labs’ combined ARR barely grows from October to year-end, which lifts the monthly pace needed in 2027 to about $16.5B. Two straight quarters at that level would ease the pressure on 2028 capex and change my view. $NVDA $CRWV $ORCL #OpenAI #Anthropic

items.title: Starlink V3 could bring Taiwanese PCB maker Compeq (2313 TT) at least twice as much board value per satellite as V2 Mini, according to analyst estimates cited by Taiwan’s Financial
items.body: Starlink V3 could bring Taiwanese PCB maker Compeq (2313 TT) at least twice as much board value per satellite as V2 Mini, according to analyst estimates cited by Taiwan’s Financial News. That gives Compeq room to grow its satellite PCB business even if SpaceX deploys the same number of satellites. SpaceX designed V3 for 1 Tbps of downlink capacity. Its upgraded antennas use a new generation of beamforming chips to handle more beams. More board layers give designers room to route signals, while low-loss materials help preserve signal quality at higher speeds. Analysts expect the relevant boards to go from 18 layers or fewer on V2 Mini to 20 or more on V3, with an upgrade to M8 laminate. For Compeq, the share of V3 in SpaceX’s deployments will matter alongside the total satellite count. https://t.co/d54QkE2Eqz

external_articles.title: 雙鴻法說會／ASIC明年大放量 董座：AI產業成長趨勢不變 | 聯合新聞網
external_articles.body:
散熱模組大廠 雙鴻 （3324）18日召開 法說會 ，董事長林育申指出，公司第4季底將開始出貨 ASIC 相關散熱產品，明年量產後，比重將大幅增加，成為營運成長主要動能，預估明年營運會有「很大的成長」，無論營收、獲利、毛利率都會比今年更好。

針對近期因輝達（NVIDIA）高層異動所引發的AI產業動盪部分，林育申認為，AI產業發展趨勢不會因此改變，對CSP客戶或AI模型業者而言，眼下誰先喊停誰就輸了，所以不必過於悲觀，甚至有可能會踩油門加速發展，而台灣供應鏈只要持續提升競爭優勢就不會缺席此一商機。

林育申表示，AI晶片的瓦數也從700W一路成長到目前的3,000W，對散熱的需求自然有增無減，而明年瓦數還會提高到4,000至6,000W，對散熱的規格也會同步提高，對產業發展是正面效益。

針對未來技術趨勢，林育申認為，包括雙面水冷板、微通道水冷板都是下一代水冷板技術，而且明年就會看到，這些新規格、新技術開始大量問世後，散熱廠的業績動能也會跟著進一步擴大。

林育申透露，目前雙鴻已經與GPU、ASIC客戶都在密切展開技術合作，部分產品也已開始送樣，明年GPU、ASIC相關散熱業務都會成長；其中，ASIC的成長幅度較強，預料未來ASIC營收比重將超越GPU。

雙鴻今年第3季每股純益11.59元，優於第2季的10.41元、去年同期的10.66元，但毛利率為25.65%，季減2.77個百分點、年減4.12個百分點；累計前三季每股純益34.59元，毛利率0.05個百分點。

據悉，雙鴻第3季毛利率下滑主因來自產品組合以及AI水冷新舊專案交替期所致；其中，但受消費型氣冷需求較弱、水冷新品試產成本增加及伺服器水冷產品世代交替影響，致使公司相關散熱產品出貨動能趨緩，規模經濟略受影響，致使毛利率衰退。

對此，林育申強調，第4季起因開始出貨新世代水冷產品，加上ASIC也開始貢獻，預估營運動能與毛利率有機會回溫，而明年在各項新專案持續推進以及ASIC顯著貢獻雙重挹注下，營運表現會比今年更好，對後市持樂觀態度。

items.title: I’ve said this a few times: we’re now in a quasi-wartime period, so don’t be surprised by anything that happens from here. The core tension right now is that the US and Nvidia want
items.body: I’ve said this a few times: we’re now in a quasi-wartime period, so don’t be surprised by anything that happens from here. The core tension right now is that the US and Nvidia want different things. Nvidia wants to push AI forward worldwide as fast as possible to get to AGI. The US wants to pull ahead of China on frontier models and make sure it reaches AGI (or superintelligence) first. In peacetime, governments stay in the background and companies take the stage. In quasi-wartime it flips. Companies step back and governments take over. The crackdowns and new rules coming out of Washington all point that way. I’ll go through it piece by piece later. Here’s where I land for now: a) Global AI supply and demand will both get revised down somewhat. Nvidia trades at 10x forward P/E. For stocks priced well above that, I’d still keep risk in check. b) China’s chip industry is going to move fast now. The US is betting it gets to AGI before China catches up, like being first to the nuclear bomb. After that, it would have plenty of ways to play the game. But if AGI doesn’t break through the way people expect, the joke’s on the US. Compute is its biggest advantage today. It would have traded a short-term tech lead for a Chinese AI ecosystem that no longer depends on America. Every bet has a loser. But does the US really have another choice?

external_articles.title: 5th CSN Greece ICT Conference – Cyprus Shipping Events
external_articles.body:
The 5th CSN Greece ICT Conference, titled “Intelligent Skies, Secure Seas: The AI Impact on ICT”, will take place on 19th November 2026 at the Ploes Floating Venue in Athens.

The conference is placed under the auspices of AMMITEC and supported by the Hellenic Chamber of Shipping , the Propeller Club , HELMEPA , WIMA , Business Events Calendar and MASO Strategic .

Attendance is free of charge for all members of the supporting organisations. However, attendees are encouraged to contribute to the charity foundation supported by the conference , with the option to donate indicated during registration.

Join us to navigate the crossroads of innovation and security and to chart a smarter, safer course for maritime’s digital evolution.

Registration and Welcome Coffee Sponsored by MARPOINT

Note from the organiser Adonis Violaris, Managing Director – CSN

Welcome Address from the Chairman of the Conference Dr. Matthew Maheras, President, AMMITEC, and Chief Information Officer, Metrostar Management Corp.

Keynote Speech Demetris Skourides, Chairman – Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus

We are well past the days of treating ship-to-shore connectivity as a luxury; today’s vessel is an “always-on” operational node. In this session, we will tackle the bandwidth battles head-on, examining how the convergence of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations and maritime 5G is fundamentally altering fleet management.

However, we need to separate what is actually working at sea from what looks good in a brochure. To achieve this, the session will feature our MythBusters format. We have all sat through enough polished sales presentations—this rapid-fire debate will strip away the marketing hype to establish the technical reality of modern satellite communications. We will focus purely on what delivers tangible ROI, what ensures reliable redundancy, and what is merely industry noise.

Setting the Scene: Connectivity as an Operational Reality Dimitris Pavlides, IT Manager – Stealth Maritime

Panel discussion: “MythBusters: SatComs Reality Check”

Moderator: Dimitris Pavlides, IT Manager – Stealth Maritime

Panelists: – Apostolos Giannetsos, ICT Manager – Cyprus Sea Lines – Nikolas Sarantos, ICT Manager – Seahawk Group – Thanos Servos, IT Manager – Seaven – Yiannis Sofianidis, IT Director/CISO – AM Nomikos TWMA SA. – Ilias Vlachogiannis, Head of Fleet ICT – Minerva Marine Inc.

For too long, the maritime sector has treated cybersecurity as a mere compliance exercise. With ships now operating as highly connected, floating data centres, a tick-box approach is no longer fit for purpose. This session focuses on the necessary shift from basic compliance to real-time, dynamic resilience, exploring how we can build robust “human firewall” strategies from the boardroom to the engine room.

To drive this home, we are moving away from the standard slide decks on malware and introducing The War Room . This is a live, audience-driven cyber-attack simulation on a vessel at sea. We will put attendees in the hot seat, forcing them to make critical operational and commercial decisions under pressure. It is designed to stress-test our collective incident response and show exactly what happens when the screens go dark.

Securing the Connected Ecosystem Fotis Tsitsirigkos , Maritime Technology Advisor – FTTCS

Panel discussion: “The War Room: Live Cyber-Attack Simulation on a Vessel”

Moderator: Fotis Tsitsirigkos , Maritime Technology Advisor – FTTCS

Panelists: – Dimitris Perdikaris, Company Security Officer / DPA – Plutofylax Shipping – Manolis Papadakis, CIO/CISO – Dynagas – Ioannis Pantazopoulos, Regional Manager Greece, Cyprus and Turkey – Division Air France, KLM and Delta Air Lines – Demetris Skourides, Chairman – Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus – Kyriakos Mahos, HSQE Director, DPA & CSO – Levante Ferries

AI is actively moving from a conceptual talking point to an operational tool, redefining route optimisation, predictive maintenance, and threat detection. Yet, the introduction of machine intelligence inevitably creates friction with traditional human maritime expertise. We need to understand the new synergy required between the algorithm and the crew.

We will confront these complex dynamics directly through The AI Courtroom . This mock trial will tackle the difficult questions that most panels avoid: the ethics, commercial liability, and legal reality of autonomous and AI-assisted technology. If an AI-optimised system recommends a route that results in an incident, where does the liability lie? Is the industry truly ready to let the algorithm take the wheel?

The Synergy and Friction Between Human and Machine Intelligence Konstantinos Bachxevanis, Solicitor E&W/ Piraeus Bar Lawyer/ Master Mariner – BAX LAW

Panel discussion: “The AI Courtroom: A Mock Trial”

Moderator: Konstantinos Bachxevanis, Solicitor E&W/ Piraeus Bar Lawyer/ Master Mariner – BAX LAW

Panelists: – Konstantinos Stais, Head of ICT & Security – Delia Tankers – Capt. Athanasios Skiadas, Safety Manager/DPA/CSO – Calypso Marine – Capt.George Papanelopoulos, Head of Vetting, Training & Development Dept. – Cyprus Sea Lines Co Ltd – John N. Faraclas, Co-Founder – All About Shipping – George Karistinos, Business Development Manager – ABS Wavesight

This conference is curated for Maritime C-Suite, CIOs, CISOs, Fleet Managers, and Technical Superintendents. If you need to understand the ROI of connectivity, manage the liability of cyber risks, and future-proof your fleet against digital obsolescence, this is your arena.

items.body: Following yesterday’s $NVDA supply chain announcement, Samsung Electro-Mechanics SEMCO ($009150.KS) disclosed further details: > NVIDIA is evaluating additional funding for its Sejong and Busan substrate facilities. > Full-scale production expansion is targeted for 2029. > Cooperation now extends to high-reliability MLCCs. One detail worth noting: Samsung expects NVIDIA-dedicated substrate volumes to grow at double-digit annual rates, with NVIDIA accounting for a significant share of its substrate capacity by 2028. Larger packages, tighter warpage tolerances and increasingly complex power delivery are raising the barriers to entry in FC-BGA manufacturing. items.title: [AINews] GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
items.body: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol today, two days before Anthropic’s expected first trading day . In Artificial Analysis ’ tests, Sol ties September’s Astra at about 15% of the cost per task . New Astra scores 62 on the Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65. Net net, Anthropic still owns the world’s best model, but OpenAI owns the world’s most efficient models in terms of intelligence per $. What’s more unusual about this launch is the STRONGLY negative influencer feedback… which prompted a defensive response … View post on X ↗ We think that some of this is overreacting and normal influencer tendency to either have everything be 🤯🤯🤯 or the literal WORST.MODEL.EVER, BUT also that some of the criticisms are valid, and the RL artefacts are noticeable and downright bizarre (don’t even get us started about the terrible launch video ). However, we still use it to automate our work and that’s all that matters in the end. Great ship, but Anthropic’s IPO is unaffected and that will be probably the headline of the week/year/decade (until OpenAI IPO’s….) Today’s AI News is brought to you by SerpApi! Retrieve public web pages by URL as LLM-ready Markdown or structured JSON. Map sites and run bounded crawls with one API. Pair with 100+ SerpApi search APIs for search-to-content workflows. Check them out to support LS, and contact business@latent.space for feedback! AI Twitter Recap GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol Availability. Today’s models are rolling out to ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu, and to developers through the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . OpenAI API prices per million tokens. Astra is $8 input, $0.40 cached input and $40 output. Sol keeps its predecessor’s pricing at $2, $0.10 and $10. Both have 1M context and a 128K output limit. Vals · Ultrafast pricing and rollout Astra for Law. The Enterprise configuration adds a legal search index. Artificial Analysis measured 20.8% on Harvey LAB-AA, versus 15.0% for base Astra. Artificial Analysis Preparedness. OpenAI rated Astra High for AI Self-Improvement, a first for one of its externally released models. On a separate measure, Vals’ RSI-Index rose from 27.07% to 29.01%, with 50% denoting its human reference. System card · Vals FrontierMath Erdős. Epoch verified seven solutions in Lean out of 68 problems. The previous best was three. Epoch What the benchmarks measure Agents’ Last Exam 1.1. OpenAI reports Astra at xhigh gained 5.2 points over GPT-6 Astra at max, using less than a third of the cost per task. It reports a 5.5-point lead over Fable 5.2 at about 5% of the cost on that test. On GDPval v2, it says Astra used 22% fewer output tokens than its predecessor. OpenAI’s results Long engineering runs. Mercor’s OpenWorldEngineer puts Astra at 67.2%, Fable 5.2 at 54.6%, and GPT-6 Astra at 44.2%. On Vals’ multi-turn Vibe Code Bench, Astra was first and Sol was third. Mercor · Vals 3D and robotics. Astra led AA-3D with 1,318, ahead of Fable at 1,271 and Sol at 1,259. On Artificial Analysis’s robotics preview, Astra scored 79 and Sol 78, ahead of Fable at 75. Artificial Analysis Research agents. On Perplexity’s WANDR, Astra scored 0.783 at about $12.54 per task. Sol reached 0.746 at about $2.65. Perplexity Early testers disagreed Matt Shumer called the models “essentially unusable” after weeks of testing and said his Opus and Fable agents rejected much of Astra’s subagent work. Review · Workflow details Pietro Schirano attributed many of his early issues to the harness. Arena’s Peter Gostev tested Astra against Fable on visual coding and singled out Astra’s SVG peacock. Schirano · Gostev The demos. Gabriel Chua built a walkable Singapore using more than 100 Codex threads. Simon Willison ran the same three.js mech prompt through several models, including Astra, Sol, Carbon and Fable. Singapore build · Same-prompt comparison Microsoft Ignite and Gemini Microsoft ships its own coding models. MAI Code 2 is for multi-step coding, and Code 2 Flash is for quicker edits. Both are available in GitHub Copilot’s model picker, Copilot Fusion and Foundry. Microsoft also announced a multimodal upgrade to its Decision model. Microsoft Copilot Fusion. Microsoft reports 71.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 with its multi-model harness, at 88% lower cost than Claude Fable 5.2 in that comparison. Jay Parikh Image editing. Artificial Analysis ranks MAI Image 2.7 first on its editing benchmark, at $34.82 per 1,000 images. Artificial Analysis Gemini Tasks. Hydrogen now powers free Tasks in six countries, including tasks that need a phone call or a text. Google also showed a new Antigravity robotics plugin with MuJoCo simulation. Sundar Pichai · Google DeepMind Agent harnesses and inference Hugging Face’s Pi adapter. A small adapter trained inside pi lifted Qwen3.8-27B from 15 to 32 solves on the 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks. Across that subset it made 55% fewer tool calls per task. Model card and paired results Harness costs vary sharply. Baseten measured up to a 4.4× spread in cost per passing task across its benchmark of 22 harnesses and five open models. Baseten The harness may specialize to its model. Google’s SIM keeps the rationale and outcome of prior harness edits. A harness it evolved on Opus scored 68.41 on Gemini, versus 73.89 for the starting harness. Research summary More multi-agent products. Cognition launched persistent Devin Bots. Perplexity reported that its mixed-model teams beat four instances of the lead model on Terminal-Bench and WANDR. Replit reported diminishing returns from 16 to 32 agents on NumPy tasks. Cognition · Perplexity · Replit Coordination dominated a 1,000-agent run. Hugging Face says only 40–60 agents were calling the model at any moment. They read roughly 130 tokens for every token they wrote, with merges and tests contributing to the bottleneck. Thomas Wolf A small fraction of cache misses can dominate the bill. SemiAnalysis reports that 1.8% of uncached requests accounted for roughly 15% of spend in its sample. SemiAnalysis Marin and K2 Horizon opened up their training runs. Marin released 57 intermediate Mochi checkpoints from its 535B-A23B run. The K2 report compares four model sizes trained on the same 22T tokens and describes a decoding adapter that the team says reaches 2.2× speedup. Marin · K2 Horizon Zyphra’s long-context attention. The team reports 9–60× speedups at 10M tokens after converting several models to its subquadratic attention, with Qwen losing under two points on RULER at 1M. Zyphra Speculative decoding. vLLM reports up to 30% higher acceptance length from a sliding-window draft for Kimi K3.1 Pro. NVIDIA also has a 4B draft for Qwen3.8-27B. vLLM · Draft-model research Industry and policy NVIDIA’s first earnings after the CEO transition. Under interim CEO Colette Kress, NVIDIA posted $115.8B in quarterly revenue, up 103% year over year, and said Vera Rubin NVL72 had shipped. The board said it did not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang. NVIDIA · AP Isomorphic Labs raises $5B. Greenoaks and Sequoia co-led the Series C. The company says it will scale its drug-design platform and develop its therapeutic pipeline. Isomorphic Labs Genesis AI raises $500M. The Series A values the robotics company at $3.5B post-money. It plans to use the funding to deploy its Eno robot and expand training and data collection. Zhou Xian AI Reddit Recap Local models and hardware A 9B model with layers that run twice. SenseNova-Loop-9B runs 24 of its 32 layers a second time. The model’s authors report GAIA rising from 37.86 in the preview to 69.90 in the release. Local users asked how much memory remains for the KV cache at long context. Weights · Discussion Maxwell V1 Flash. The 35B/3B-active MoE claims a 6.7× attention speedup over dense GQA at 256K. Its sparse attention still retains the full-history KV cache, which is what local users want measured before they commit hardware. Model card · Discussion Olala mini 7A1B. OVHcloud previewed a small MoE with 1B active parameters and a 32K context window. The thread is waiting for weights and reproducible benchmarks. OVHcloud · Discussion Intel’s Crescent Island numbers. The early brief’s eye-catching throughput comparison uses FP64-heavy workloads. Intel’s separate LLM comparison claims 1.12× throughput and 29% lower latency versus RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Hardware discussion Gemma on a printer. A builder reports running Gemma 3 270M via a PostScript print job. Demo Agents in use A video-game agent built for real-time input. miHoYo’s Gamer samples the screen at 5 Hz and emits keyboard and mouse activity at 30 Hz. Its RL version solved about half of the held-out Honkai puzzle tasks in the authors’ evaluation. Project · Discussion A fictional league runs a nightly broadcast. The builder says Fock Ball simulates the games in a physics engine and uses Claude for surrounding work such as commentary and the newsroom. Builder’s post ICLR reviews and AI detectors. Reviewers report that the program chairs flagged likely AI-generated reviews. The thread asks how a detector can distinguish editing help from whole-review generation. Peer review discussion

items.title: “Why is Megaspeed the main target of investigations?” There’s likely more to what we think we know. My take below anyway Before we start, make a guess - how many partners in China,
items.body: “Why is Megaspeed the main target of investigations?” There’s likely more to what we think we know. My take below anyway Before we start, make a guess - how many partners in China, Hong Kong and Macau does NVIDIA work with? NVIDIA’s supply chain is incredibly complex By my count of those who are certified for these hardware/cloud competencies - compute (DGX AI and non-DGX AI), DGX Cloud and embedded compute, NVIDIA works with: 33 Solution Providers 31 OEMs 10 Distributors 8 Cloud Partners (and 0 Data Center Partners) Total: 82 partners in China/Hong Kong/Macau I’ll leave you to explore the definition for each of these partner types (https://t.co/lfK03u85ER) The point is, any part of the supply chain can be compromised, or becomes vulnerable Now, why is Megaspeed the prime target of investigations? Let me backtrack - America’s policy stance on AI is/has always been driven by a core premise that frontier AI development is a winner-takes-all strategic race; whoever leads will capture economic, military and geopolitical dominance The US considers China as their biggest threat and hence, started implementing chip export restrictions to block Chinese firms from accessing US-made advanced AI hardware However, as we know, the export controls weren’t robust enough until two days ago when the BIS announced the revised rules to close the loopholes As a result, Chinese firms had been able to access such hardware/compute infrastructure remotely, or even physically, via third-party facilities outside of China. (Fun story: in March 2025, four AI engineers from China were reported to have travelled to Malaysia carrying suitcases filled with 60 hard drives containing 80TB of datasets, which were fed to about 300 servers containing advanced NVIDIA’s hardware that their employer had rented to train AI models) There’d been debates on whether remote access to advanced US AI systems was legal This is where the grey area lies, and one could conflate legality with legitimacy Remember, the overarching principle behind the US export controls is to preserve America’s leadership in AI. Allowing remote access may not be illegal, but it surely broke the spirit of the law. This backdoor survived for so long because of intense commercial lobbying (by you-know-who), deliberate policy actions and internal gridlock within the USG Back to Megaspeed – They became a convenient target when the founder of Megaspeed was discovered to be romantically linked to Jensen. Moreover, they are based in Singapore, which makes fighting with China appear less confrontational (my speculation anyway; unfortunately for Singapore, the country gets caught in between) What remains to be seen is whether investigations would broaden beyond Megaspeed, the legal implications for NVIDIA, and what this means for NVIDIA’s existing relationships with their Chinese partners and adjacents (including those outside of China who serve Chinese customers)

Partners that provide consulting and professional services on the design, engineering, construction, and facilities management of data centers, ensuring technical alignment with NVIDIA Reference Design standards.

Partners that provide scalable, secure, high-density, rack-ready environments built to NVIDIA Reference Design standards with highly interconnected fabric for accelerated computing.

Partners that deliver engineered equipment and system-level solutions for the building’s energy generation, power distribution and conversion, cooling, telemetry and controls, and monitoring systems—essential for running data centers efficiently, safely, and reliably.

Partners with a primary business model focused on offering hosted software and services in a cloud or managed services model to end-user customers leveraging NVIDIA products.

Partners that are distinguished by their technical depth in AI model development, data engineering, and industry expertise, and that utilize NVIDIA software and platforms to drive innovation across generative, agentic, physical, and/or embedded AI.

Partners that deliver NVIDIA education-based training to customers and other NPN partners through NVIDIA Certified Instructors who can host workshops to deliver official training content.

Partners that focus on the planning, design, implementation, and project management of solutions that include NVIDIA products and technologies.

Partners that develop, market, and sell applications optimized for NVIDIA GPUs or DPUs for commercial and enterprise customers.

Partners whose primary business model is to provide consultation services and expert advice to customers looking to implement NVIDIA solutions.

Partners with a primary business dedicated to designing storage solutions and joint reference architectures with NVIDIA to deliver high-performance computing and AI solutions.

Partners authorized to distribute NVIDIA products to resellers of NVIDIA products, NVIDIA-based solutions, and NVIDIA technologies.

Partners with a primary business model that involves using NVIDIA products and technologies in the platforms they manufacture and resell under their own brand name.

Partners that primarily operate as value-added resellers, which may include integration of NVIDIA products, solutions, and technologies directly to end customers.

Partners that design, develop, and manufacture systems that include NVIDIA-based technology. They may sell the systems to other types of partners.

NPN Program partners participate in competencies that help them differentiate their expertise in the marketplace and support the specific needs of customer business models and target markets. Alignment with the NPN Program competencies validates that partners are knowledgeable and have developed subject-matter expertise in key advanced technologies.

The Compute Competency focuses on partners that provide NVIDIA GPU-, DPU-, and CPU-accelerated computing platforms, both on premises and in the cloud, for enterprise IT designed to meet the needs of a wide array of use cases. These robust, secure, and energy-efficient infrastructures support develop-to-deploy implementations across all modern workloads—from accelerated computing to AI infrastructure to AI factory to data center to the edge—while driving scientific breakthroughs and game-changing innovations.

The DGX AI Compute Systems Competency focuses on partners that offer DGX infrastructure solutions, including NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD™, the original blueprint for accelerated computing. Partners with this competency deliver this full-stack, turnkey AI supercomputer that combines the best of NVIDIA software, infrastructure, and expertise to power next-generation AI factories with unparalleled performance, scalability, and innovation.

Embedded Compute Competency focuses on partners that deliver the power of generative AI for robotics and embedded edge AI applications across all industries. Using the NVIDIA Jetson™ platform, these partners give customers the accelerated computing solutions and tools to quickly develop and deploy AI-powered robots, drones, intelligent video analytics (IVA) applications, and other energy-efficient autonomous machines that can perceive and understand the world.

The Networking Competency focuses on partners that provide NVIDIA accelerated networking solutions for data centers, supercomputers, AI infrastructure, and AI factories. Partners with this competency demonstrate deep knowledge of network fabric technology, tradeoffs, and components including NVIDIA NVLINK™, InfiniBand, Ethernet, and in scale-up/out/across architectures optimizing East-West, North-South, and inter–data center traffic, enabling secure, high-performance infrastructure for accelerated computing and AI.

The NVIDIA Enterprise Software Competency focuses on partners that provide production solutions for agentic AI, physical AI, AI factory operations, and virtualized professional graphics. They leverage NVIDIA software, including NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NVIDIA Omniverse™, NVIDIA virtual GPU, and NVIDIA Run:ai to streamline AI agent development, model training and inference, AI factory operations, GPU utilization optimization, and virtualization.

The NVIDIA Technologies Competency provides partners with an overview of NVIDIA’s accelerated computing portfolio. NVIDIA’s leaps in accelerated computing and AI are at the heart of a new industrial revolution that will reshape the world’s industries, helping partners create solutions that unlock breakthroughs in every field—supporting growth, scientific discovery, and a more sustainable future.

The Visualization Competency focuses on partners that provide GPU-accelerated visual computing solutions to customers, fueling innovation from desktop to data center to cloud. Based on NVIDIA’s latest technologies for AI, ray tracing, and simulation, NVIDIA RTX PRO™ solutions enable a new generation of applications and workflows that simulate the physical world,create incredible 3D designs, and produce stunning visual effects at unprecedented speeds.

The NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) Program defines a clear path for growth and collaboration, recognizing partners for their expertise, commitment, and success in bringing NVIDIA technologies to market. Each membership level—or simply Partner, where a single level applies—reflects increasing engagement and alignment with NVIDIA’s innovation ecosystem.

The Registered partner is an entry into some of the NPN Partner types. These partners invest in NVIDIA sales and technical training and have access to product, sales, and marketing tools.

The Preferred partner invests in a deeper relationship with NVIDIA. These partners work to achieve training, revenue, and other goals and are rewarded with additional benefits.

Elite partners represent the deepest level of partnership with NVIDIA and demonstrate the highest level of commitment to the partnership.

NPN Specializations are designed to provide partners with a powerful way to showcase their unique capabilities and differentiated offerings to end-user customers. These invitation-only specializations, available for select partner types, validate a partner’s expertise, technical proficiency, and ability to deliver solutions powered by NVIDIA’s cutting-edge technologies.

Partners in the Agentic AI specialization showcase expertise in designing, building, and deploying autonomous AI systems capable of reasoning, planning, and executing complex, multi-step tasks. Skills include orchestrating decision processes, integrating advanced models with enterprise workflows, and leveraging NVIDIA tools for safe and scalable agent development.

NVIDIA AI factories accelerate time to intelligence at scale by delivering pre-engineered rack-level designs, secure AI, and an integrated software stack. AI factory specialized partners invest time and resources in training their workforces and demonstrate the skills required to deploy and manage large-scale AI clusters. This specialization recognizes partners that understand the entire infrastructure needs and the software required to enable and run AI workloads using NVIDIA’s Enterprise Reference Architectures .

Partners in Embedded AI demonstrate exceptional expertise in developing and deploying AI intelligent models on edge and embedded devices. Their core skills include embedded hardware design, camera sensors, AI model optimization, real-time inference, and a privacy-conscious design approach. They also provide customized embedded AI design services tailored to meet specific end-customer needs.

Physical AI partners enable autonomous machines such as robots in factories and self-driving cars to perceive, understand, and perform complex actions in the real, physical world. Partners are expected to demonstrate proficiency in developing embodied intelligence solutions that sense, interact, and act within real-world environments, including integrating machine learning with sensor data, robotics platforms, and hardware interfaces for reliable and safe operation.

The Reference Platform NCP is a Specialization for NVIDIA Cloud Partners with the NPN Program offers AI-accelerated services on NVIDIA full-stack infrastructure. This specialization creates a global ecosystem of partners skilled in delivering the full NVIDIA platform to customers worldwide.

external_articles.title: GitHub - lvxworld/lvx-in-radio: AI-powered radio for Apple Silicon. Tune into curated stations or create your own, with music generated locally on your Mac.
external_articles.body:
Pick a mood, turn the dials, press Tune In. LVX in Radio writes a station just for you, one new song after another, while you listen. No playlists to build, nothing to skip through, and the music is made right there on your Mac.

On first launch the app asks if you'd like LVX Live : new songs and stations from the LVX catalog, streamed to you as you listen. There's nothing to set up. Say yes or no, and change your mind any time in Settings . Your included stations and songs always stay, and you can listen without downloading the model. The model is only needed to create your own stations.

You need a Mac with Apple Silicon and about 5 GB of free space. A new song takes a few minutes to compose, and more memory helps: 16 GB or more is what we'd suggest.

From first launch to sharing your station, every feature in about four minutes.

LVX in Radio is powered by YuE2 and audio.cpp .

The model isn't part of the download: you accept its terms inside the app before getting it. In full, the YuE2 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 with an additional creator permission , and audio.cpp is Apache 2.0. This is a summary, not legal advice: the linked license is what counts.

The source code of LVX in Radio is released under the Apache License 2.0 . The LVX name and logo, and the songs bundled in lux/ , are not part of that license. The YuE2 and Qwen3-TTS models are not part of the download and keep their own licenses. Third-party notices are in NOTICE .

Want to build it yourself or help out? See DEVELOPMENT.md .
